Booked a suite at Affinia and walked into a dated room that smelled faintly of old carpet. AC rattled all night, and housekeeping never replenished the tiny shampoo bottles. For the price, the staff were polite but overwhelmed--truly underwhelming stay.

Booked the Allegro for a weekend getaway and left pretty let down. The lobby looks great in photos but the room was worn out, the AC rattled all night, and the front desk barely acknowledged us. Not worth the price, honestly. Won't be back.

The location was great, but that's about all this place has going for it. Our room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and the staff acted like we were bothering them. For these prices, I expected a lot more.

We booked the Ambassador expecting a nice anniversary getaway, but it fell flat. The room was stifling hot, the AC barely worked, and housekeeping never showed up until we called twice. The bar was understaffed and drinks took forever. Not worth the hype or the price.

The Conrad felt more like a corporate checkbox than a luxury escape. Our room had a stale odor, AC rattled all night, and housekeeping missed turn-down despite asking twice. Staff were polite but utterly indifferent--we expected far more for the price.

I really wanted to love the Fairmont, but our anniversary stay fell flat. The room felt dated, the air conditioning was noisy all night, and the staff seemed rushed and indifferent when we asked for a quiet floor. For the price, I expected far more polish.

The room smelled like stale smoke and the 'rock star' service was a myth--waited 40 minutes at the front desk while staff gossiped. Pool was packed with non-guests, and the bar overcharged for flat drinks. Definitely not worth the hype for this price.

Booked a king room expecting Hilton standards, but the air conditioning rattled all night, the hallway smelled like old carpet, and the front desk seemed annoyed by every question. For the price, I've had better stays at mid-range motels. Won't be returning.

The room smelled musty and the AC rattled all night, so I barely slept. Staff were polite but shrugged off the issues, and the breakfast was cold and picked over by 8 AM. Really disappointed for what we paid.

Booked the Hyatt for a weekend getaway and left pretty deflated. The room was tired, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that smelled musty. Staff seemed overwhelmed at check-in, and the breakfast buffet was cold and overpriced--definitely not worth the hype.

The 'luxury' felt like a facade--our room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping never replaced towels. Staff were polite but useless when we asked for a late checkout. For this price, utter disappointment.

Honestly, the James felt more like a flashy hostel than a luxury hotel. The room was impossibly small, the walls paper-thin, and I could hear every door slam until 3 AM. Staff were polite but useless when I asked for a quiet room. Not worth the premium price.

I expected old-school charm but got peeling wallpaper, a broken AC that cycled all night, and staff who shrugged at the noise from the street. Location is fine, but for the price, this place needs serious maintenance. I left exhausted and disappointed.

Stayed at Hotel Monaco expecting a boutique treat, but the room felt worn and the AC rattled all night. Staff were polite but indifferent, and breakfast was overpriced for what you got. Not worth the hype or the price tag.

The room was freezing and the AC unit rattled all night, so sleep was impossible. Service felt robotic and distant, and housekeeping never replaced the towels. For these rates, I expected far more polish. Sadly, left disappointed.

The location is fine, but the room was noisy all night and the AC barely worked. Staff seemed overwhelmed and forgot our wake-up call. For these prices, I expected way more polish. Left feeling pretty let down overall.

Disappointing stay--the room was dated and smelled musty, and housekeeping never restocked our towels. Check-in was slow despite booking directly, and the AC barely worked. For the price, I expected far more polish. Probably won't return.

Stayed here for a conference and left feeling underwhelmed. The room was tired, with scuffed furniture and a view of a wall. Staff were polite but painfully slow, and the so-called luxury breakfast was cold and overpriced. For this price tag, I expected far more polish.

The location is fine, but that's about it. Our room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping never replaced the towels. Front desk was polite but shrugged off every complaint. For the price, this felt like a basic chain, not a Swissotel. Won't be back.

I booked the Talbott expecting charm, but the room felt tired and the walls paper-thin--heard every hallway conversation until 2 a.m. Staff was polite but slow, and breakfast was lukewarm at best. Not worth the price tag.

The room smelled musty, the air conditioning clanked all night, and housekeeping never replaced our towels despite calling twice. The lobby looks great in photos, but the hallways are dingy and the hallway noise is relentless. Not worth the price.

Booked the Allegro for a weekend getaway and left pretty let down. Room was worn, the AC rattled all night, and the 'helpful' front desk seemed annoyed every time I asked a basic question. Not worth the hype or the price.

We booked a superior room with a sea view, but got a cramped box facing a brick wall. The front desk shrugged and said 'full occupancy.' Breakfast was cold scrambled eggs and stale pastries, not worth the €25. For these prices, absolutely not.

The location was the only saving grace. Room was tired, the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping ignored our do-not-disturb sign twice. Front desk shrugged off the noise complaint. Paid way too much for what felt like a budget stay. Won't be back.

The Conrad felt like a letdown for the price. Check-in was painfully slow, the room had a musty smell, and housekeeping never came despite asking twice. The location is great, but that doesn't fix the dated bathroom or rude front desk.

The Fairmont's grandeur fades fast--our room was tired, with a view of an air shaft and a bathroom that smelled musty all weekend. Staff were polite but stretched thin, making us wait 20 minutes for a simple ice refill. For the price, this felt like a letdown.

Booked a 'Sound of Your Stay' package but the guitar in the room was locked away, staff seemed annoyed when I asked about it. Room felt worn, AC rattled all night, and the pool had a weird smell. Not the vibe you'd expect from this brand.

The room was fine at first glance, but the air conditioning rattled all night and the hallway noise made sleep impossible. Staff seemed overwhelmed at check-in, and the breakfast buffet ran out of everything by 8 AM. Not the Hilton standard I expected.

Stayed here for a conference and left genuinely underwhelmed. The room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping never replaced our towels. Overpriced for what feels like a tired property that's clearly seen better days.

Booked the Intercontinental expecting luxury, but the room felt tired, the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping ignored our do-not-disturb sign. Overpriced and underwhelming for the brand name.

Checked in expecting the James' usual polish, but our room smelled musty, the AC rattled nonstop, and housekeeping skipped us entirely one day. For $400 a night, that's just insulting--service felt indifferent, and the rooftop bar was overcrowded. Disappointed.

The staff were indifferent at best and the room felt tired, with a broken hairdryer and stained carpet. For these prices, I expected far more polish--definitely left feeling underwhelmed and overcharged.
The hype is all wrong for this place. Room was tiny, walls paper-thin, and the 'vibe' couldn't mask the stale smell and rude front desk. Paid a fortune for a headache. Never again.

The Omni is really showing its age. The hallway smelled like old carpet and the air conditioner rattled all night, making sleep impossible. Staff were polite but offered little help. Definitely not worth the premium price.

Booked a city view but got a parking lot; AC sounded like a jet engine and the hallways smelled like old fries. Staff were polite but the whole stay felt rundown and overpriced for what we got.

Booked the Sofitel expecting Parisian elegance, but got worn carpets, a broken mini-bar, and staff who seemed annoyed by every request. The 'quiet' room faced a jackhammer. Not worth the premium--I'd pick a clean mid-range hotel next time.

The air conditioning barely worked and the hallways smelled like stale cigarettes. Staff were polite but painfully slow to respond when our sink clogged. Definitely not worth the premium price for such a worn-down room.

The beds were rock hard and the walls paper-thin; I heard every elevator ding and hallway conversation. Service felt indifferent and our room wasn't ready until past check-in. Disappointing for the price.
Room smelled like stale smoke and the AC rattled all night. Front desk shrugged when I asked to switch. Paid way too much for a broken shower head and paper-thin walls. Won't be back.

The location is great, but the room was dated and the bathroom smelled musty. Staff were indifferent when I complained, and the thin walls meant I heard every word from the neighbors. Left feeling ripped off.

The location was lovely, but the hotel itself feels tired and dated. The air conditioning barely worked, breakfast was chaotic, and our room smelled musty. Definitely not worth the premium price we paid.

The hallways smelled like stale cigarette smoke, and housekeeping ignored our request for extra towels twice. Honestly, for these prices, the threadbare carpets and lukewarm shower were a total letdown. We left feeling ripped off.

The air conditioning barely worked and the hallway smelled like stale cigarettes. For the price, the paper-thin walls and worn-out furniture felt like a real rip-off. I expected so much more.
Service was indifferent and the room felt dated, with a broken AC that took hours to fix. The noise from the bar below made rest impossible, and I left feeling ripped off for the price.

The staff were lovely, but felt like they were working against the building. Bathroom had a persistent musty smell and the hallways were loud until 3 AM. Not the chic, romantic escape I'd hoped for at this price.
The Omni looked grand in photos, but our room was dated, with a musty smell and paper-thin walls. Staff were polite but slow, and the overpriced valet was a joke. Left feeling ripped off.

The location is convenient, but the room felt tired and the hallway noise was relentless. The promised 'city view' was mostly a brick wall, and breakfast was a sad, lukewarm afterthought. Overall, this stay was a miss for the price.

The room's worn furniture and flickering bathroom light set the tone. Staff seemed overwhelmed, and the AC rattled all night. Honestly expected far more polish from a Sheraton--left frustrated and disappointed.

The rooms are stunning, but the staff seemed overwhelmed and indifferent during our entire stay. We waited over an hour for luggage delivery, and the pool was inexplicably closed for a private event without notice. Expected far more for the price.

The location is fantastic, but that's where the positives end. Our room felt tired, the air conditioning was broken, and housekeeping never replaced the towels. A truly disappointing stay for the price.

The room was worn and the AC rattled all night, plus the 'city view' was a brick wall. Staff seemed annoyed by basic requests, so I'd skip this place next time.

The room was so noisy my neighbor's phone conversation kept me up half the night. Staff seemed annoyed when I asked for towels, and the AC barely worked, making it stuffy. Beautiful lobby, but that's where it ends. Not worth it.

The location was stunning, but that's where the magic ended. Our room smelled musty, the air conditioning barely worked, and the breakfast buffet was lukewarm and chaotic every single morning. Expected so much more for the price.

The breakfast buffet was a chaotic free-for-all with empty chafing dishes, and housekeeping never once replenished our towels despite the 'do not disturb' sign we never hung. Save your money for somewhere that actually cares about guests.

The service was painfully slow and the staff seemed overwhelmed, though the room itself was clean. For these prices, the dated hallway carpet and the busted espresso machine in the cafe were a real letdown. I expected far more polish.

My anniversary dinner reservation was lost, and the front desk shrugged it off. The room's air conditioning rattled all night, and housekeeping forgot our turn-down service. For this price, I expected polish, not problems.
The room was tired and the AC sounded like a jet engine all night. Staff were indifferent when I complained, and the pool felt more like a crowded public bath. Left with a sour taste for the price.

The room was tired and smelled musty, and the air conditioning rattled all night. The front desk staff were polite but couldn't fix the noise, and breakfast was a chaotic, understocked scramble. Not the Hilton standard I remember.

The staff were lovely, but the room felt dated and smelled musty. The AC was loud all night, and the breakfast buffet was a sad, overpriced spread. Not the Hyatt standard I expected at all.

Disappointed. Check-in took forever, the room smelled musty, and housekeeping forgot towels twice. For this price, I expect the 'luxury' they advertise, not worn carpets and lukewarm water. Won't be back.

Checked in after 4 PM only to find our room wasn't ready, and the front desk was indifferent when we complained. The air conditioning rattled all night, and the overpriced breakfast buffet was cold and stale. Not worth the hype.

The grand lobby promised luxury, but our room smelled of damp carpet and the AC rattled all night. Breakfast was chaos, and staff seemed annoyed by basic requests. Not the Sofitel standard I remember.

The room felt dated and the air conditioning rattled all night, making sleep impossible. Breakfast was a chaotic stampede with lukewarm food, and the front desk seemed annoyed by every request--hardly the standard you'd expect from this name.

The Talbotts antique charm wore thin fast--our 'deluxe' room was cramped, the AC rattled all night, and the front desk shrugged off our noise complaints. Overpriced and underwhelming; we cut our stay short.

My only regret is that I booked just one night at Affinia--I could have happily holed up for a week. The room was a quiet sanctuary despite being on a busy street; I never heard a peep from neighbors or traffic, and the blackout curtains did their job perfectly. I slept like a log on that firm-but-plush bed, waking only to the sun sneaking past the edges. Wi-Fi was fast and stable the whole time, no annoying login drops, which meant I actually finished my emails instead of rage-quitting. Location was ideal for walking everywhere, and the front desk even remembered my name the next morning. It felt less like a chain and more like a well-run boutique. I'm already checking dates for a return trip.

I wasn't expecting much from a mid-range hotel, but the Allegro genuinely surprised me. I slept like a log--the blackout curtains did their job, and the mattress had that perfect firm-but-plush balance. The WiFi held up even when I was streaming late at night, which is more than I can say for most places. My room was spotless: no dust on the baseboards, fresh-smelling linens, and a bathroom that looked like it had been scrubbed that morning. As for the decor, it's a bit of a time capsule--think early 2000s business chic with dark wood and geometric patterns--but it's well-maintained and has its own quiet charm. The location was ideal for walking to dinner and the staff at the front desk were genuinely warm. I'd book again without hesitation.

My stay at the Hotel Amalfi was genuinely relaxing, and it's rare I find a city hotel that hits this many notes so well. I was a bit worried about street noise given the location, but our room faced the inner courtyard and it was wonderfully quiet--I slept through all eight hours without a single interruption. The Wi-Fi was solid too, which mattered since I had to answer a few work emails; no dropped connections, and the speed was plenty for video calls. Breakfast was a pleasant surprise: fresh pastries, decent coffee, eggs made to order, and a nice spread of local cheeses. The room itself was spotless, with crisp white linens and a bathroom that looked like it had just been deep-cleaned. Honestly, the whole stay felt effortless, and I'd happily return.

My stay at the Ambassador was genuinely pleasant, and I left feeling like I'd gotten real value for the money. The room was spotless from top to bottom; I checked the corners and baseboards out of habit, and there wasn't a speck of dust anywhere. The bathroom was compact but smartly arranged, with a walk-in rain shower that had solid water pressure and thick, fluffy towels that actually dried you off. I'll admit the decor leans slightly retro--think warm woods and muted golds--but it's well-maintained and has a cozy, almost vintage charm rather than feeling tired or neglected. What impressed me most, though, was the sleep quality: the blackout curtains seal out all street light, and the mattress has that perfect firm-but-giving feel. I woke up once for water and fell right back asleep, which never happens at home. Service at check-in was quick and friendly, too. I'd happily book here again for a quiet, comfortable city break.

I booked the Conrad for a work trip and came away genuinely impressed. The staff were the standout--from the doorman remembering my name by day two to the front-desk agent who proactively rebooked my taxi when a meeting ran long. Breakfast was a cut above the usual hotel buffet: the made-to-order omelets were perfect, and the fresh pastries disappeared fast, which tells you everything. My room faced the street, yet I heard next to nothing once the window was shut; even the hallway noise was minimal. The Wi-Fi held up flawlessly through two video calls and a late-night streaming session without a single drop. It's not the flashiest property, but the consistency and care made it a restful, productive stay. I'd happily return.

I wasn't entirely sure what to expect from the Fairmont, but I left genuinely impressed--and a little sad to go. The bed was so comfortable that I slept through my alarm twice, which never happens at home. Our room faced the inner courtyard, and aside from the faint hum of the HVAC, it was wonderfully quiet; I heard zero hallway noise all weekend. The wifi held up perfectly, even during evening video calls from the lounge. If anything, the three nights felt too brief--I'd have happily stayed another day just to use the pool more. Service was attentive without hovering, and the breakfast spread was worth waking up for. Minor quibble: the bathroom door stuck slightly, but that hardly overshadowed an otherwise polished stay. I'd return in a heartbeat.

Breakfast at the Hard Rock was surprisingly solid for a hotel--think made-to-order omelets and a decent spread of fresh fruit and pastries, not just the usual sad continental slap. The staff genuinely set the tone though; the front desk crew remembered my name by day two and the bellman flagged me down with a spare umbrella when a freak storm rolled in. Honestly, for what you get--the location, the pool, the little rock-and-roll touches in the room--it felt like a fair deal, even if the weekend rate stings a bit. I was braced for thin walls and party noise, but my floor was quiet after 11, and the blackout curtains did the heavy lifting for sleep. A couple of minor wear marks in the hallway kept it from a perfect score, but I'd book again without hesitation.

The view from my room on the fifteenth floor was the standout--a sweeping panorama of the skyline that made me linger at the window every evening. The bathroom, while compact, felt wonderfully modern with a rainfall shower head and thick, plush towels that were replenished without me even asking. Staff were consistently warm and efficient, from the valet who remembered my name to the front desk who helped me rebook a dinner reservation when my schedule shifted. The decor, thankfully, doesn't lean into that tired beige-and-maroon look; instead, it's sleek with dark wood accents and tasteful, contemporary art that feels intentional rather than generic. Everything functioned flawlessly, and the bed was genuinely comfortable. A few minor scuffs on the hallway baseboards are the only hint of wear. Overall, a polished, dependable stay that exceeded my expectations--I'd happily return.

I was a little wary about booking Homewood given the price, but after three nights, I genuinely feel it was money well spent. The room wasn't just tidy; it was spotless, with fresh-smelling linens and a carpet that showed no signs of wear. The bathroom surprised me--plenty of counter space, a powerful showerhead with great water pressure, and a mirror that didn't fog up immediately, which is a small victory. What really sealed it, though, was the sleep quality. The blackout curtains did their job flawlessly, and the mattress had that perfect firmness that supports you without feeling like a board. I woke up refreshed each morning, which rarely happens in hotels. The check-in was smooth, and the lobby had a nice, quiet vibe. For a comfortable, hassle-free stay that doesn't nickel-and-dime you, this place hits the mark. I'd book again.

The Hyatt turned out to be a solid choice for my three-night stay. I was initially worried the common areas might feel tired, but the lobby and hallways have a clean, contemporary vibe that hasn't aged poorly. The room itself was quiet, and the bed was the real standout--I slept better here than I have at home in weeks, thanks to the firm mattress and blackout curtains that actually did their job. The bathroom was a pleasant surprise: a rainfall shower with strong water pressure and plenty of hot water, plus generous counter space that didn't get cluttered. Given the location and the level of comfort, I felt the rate was fair, especially compared to nearby options with less to offer. The only minor quibble was the slightly worn carpet near the door, but it didn't detract from an otherwise restful and worthwhile stay. I'd happily book here again.

Our three-night escape at the Intercontinental felt like a single, blissful afternoon--I actually found myself wishing we'd booked one more day just to linger over that skyline view from the 22nd floor. The room was immaculate, with crisp white linens and a bathroom so spotless it gleamed under the soft lighting. Housekeeping even folded my stray charging cable into a neat coil, a small touch that spoke volumes. The Wi-Fi was flawless from check-in to checkout, handling both work calls and late-night streaming without a hiccup. I'm not one to gush, but the floor-to-ceiling windows framed Lake Michigan so perfectly that I caught myself staring out more than watching TV. Genuinely, a stay that felt both too short and exactly right.

I'll admit I booked the James mostly for its address, but the stay itself turned out to be the highlight of my trip. The room wasn't huge, but it was spotless--fresh linens, no stray hairs in the bathroom, and the walk-in shower had excellent water pressure. What really stood out was the staff: from the front desk who remembered my name to the concierge who circled three under-the-radar restaurants on a map, everyone seemed genuinely happy to help. Location-wise, you're steps from the river and a short stroll to Michigan Avenue, yet the street itself felt calm at night. I slept better than I have in months. Minor quibble: the hallway ice machine was out on my floor, but that's hardly a dealbreaker. I'd return in a heartbeat, and I've already recommended it to two coworkers.

The Knickerbocker turned out to be a surprisingly restful hideaway despite its central location. Our room faced the inner courtyard, so street noise was virtually nonexistent--just the faint, pleasant hum of the city far below. The view, while not skyline-facing, had a quiet charm: rooftops and leafy terraces that felt private and calm. As for cleanliness, I'm particular, and I found zero faults; the white linens were crisp, the bathroom gleamed, and the carpets looked freshly vacuumed. The staff genuinely elevated the stay. From the doorman who remembered our name to the front desk agent who patiently rebooked our dinner reservation after a mix-up, everyone seemed to anticipate needs before we voiced them. Even the housekeeping team left a handwritten note about the weather forecast. It's rare to find that blend of efficiency and warmth. I left feeling genuinely refreshed, not just tolerated. I would absolutely return.

Stayed three nights at Hotel Monaco and came away genuinely impressed. The wifi was rock-solid from the moment I connected--I streamed video calls and work files without a single drop, which is rarer than it should be downtown. My room's bathroom had a rainfall shower with strong pressure and plenty of hot water, plus fluffy towels that actually smelled fresh. Street traffic was audible on the lower floor, but the double-paned windows and white-noise machine in the closet kept it easy to sleep by midnight. Location couldn't be beat: four blocks from the train, a two-minute walk to a decent coffee shop, and an easy stroll to the riverfront for evening walks. Staff were friendly during check-in, and the lobby's quirky decor grew on me. Would happily book again.

From the moment I checked in, the Omni felt like a calm retreat tucked right in the middle of the city's energy. My room on the 14th floor faced the lake, and I caught a spectacular sunset over the water that I didn't expect to see from a business trip. What impressed me most was how genuinely quiet it was--I heard none of the typical street noise or hallway chatter, and I slept deeply both nights, waking up refreshed before my meetings. The bathroom was a real highlight: a spacious walk-in shower with excellent water pressure, thick towels, and plenty of counter space for my toiletries. Everything felt thoughtfully designed for comfort rather than just style. The staff were warm without being intrusive, and location-wise, I could walk to dinner easily. I'd gladly book here again for a stay that balances work and relaxation effortlessly.

I wasn't expecting much from a mid-range property, but the Palmer genuinely surprised me. The decor does lean traditional--think rich wood and classic patterned carpets--yet it's been maintained so well that it feels charming rather than tired. The staff were the real highlight: the front desk remembered my name by the second day, and the bellman gave me a fantastic local eatery tip that wasn't in any guidebook. Breakfast was a pleasant affair, with made-to-order omelets and proper strong coffee, all served without a chaotic rush. Despite being near a busy avenue, my room was remarkably quiet--the double-paned windows did their job perfectly, and I slept soundly both nights. For the rate I paid, this felt like a genuine bargain, and I'd happily book here again on my next visit.

Our three-night stay at the Sheraton flew by far too quickly--the kind of visit where you find yourself lingering over coffee in the lobby just to soak up the atmosphere a little longer. The front desk team was genuinely warm, remembering our names by day two and offering a fantastic local bakery tip that became our morning ritual. We booked a high-floor room with a skyline view, and watching the city lights flicker on each evening felt like a private show. Given the plush bedding, spotless bathroom, and the surprisingly robust breakfast buffet, I'd say the rate was absolutely fair for what you get. I honestly wouldn't change a thing, except maybe steal one more night on that balcony.

My long weekend at Sofitel felt far too brief--I could have happily lingered another few days just to soak in that skyline view from my room. The floor-to-ceiling windows framed the city beautifully at both sunrise and nightfall. What truly set the stay apart, though, was the staff: every doorman, front desk agent, and housekeeper seemed genuinely invested in my comfort, remembering my name by the second morning. Breakfast was a quiet pleasure--flaky croissants, made-to-order omelets, and fresh-squeezed orange juice served in a serene dining room that never felt rushed. The bed was plush, the bathroom elegant, and the location made evening strolls effortless. I left only wishing I'd booked one more night.

Checking in was seamless--the front desk team even remembered my name the next morning, which felt personal without being overbearing. The bathroom was a genuine highlight: a rain shower with strong pressure, plus a deep soaking tub that I actually used twice. I'd booked three nights but left wishing for one more, though that's more a compliment than a complaint. The location made exploring easy, yet the rooms insulated me from street noise entirely. For the rate I paid, considering the breakfast spread and the evening turndown service with chocolates, I felt the value was solid--not a steal, but fair for the quality. Staff everywhere, from housekeeping to the concierge, were attentive without hovering. I'd gladly return, and likely will on my next trip.

My stay at Hotel Talbott was a pleasant surprise from start to finish. The front desk team greeted me with genuine warmth, even remembering my name when I returned from dinner. My room was spotless--the kind of clean that makes you want to kick off your shoes immediately. Despite being on Dearborn, I heard almost nothing from the street; the windows did wonders, and the hallway noise was minimal, which made for a truly restful night. The location is unbeatable for exploring the Loop or hopping on the riverwalk, and the Mag Mile is just a pleasant stroll away. The bathroom had great water pressure, and the bed was firm but comfortable. It's not a flashy property, but it's efficient, charming, and well-run. I'd gladly book here again for a business trip or a weekend away.

I was pleasantly surprised by how quiet my room at Affinia was--despite being on a lower floor, street noise never intruded, and the blackout curtains made for deep, restful sleep. The bathroom felt freshly updated with a rainfall showerhead and soft towels, though the vanity lighting was a touch dim for getting ready. My corner room faced the river, and watching the lights flicker on the city skyline at dusk became my favorite evening ritual. The decor skews mid-2000s boutique--dark woods and geometric accents that aren't exactly cutting-edge but remain clean and comfortable, showing minimal wear. Staff remembered my name by day two, and the lobby coffee bar was a lifesaver. Not a five-star luxury property, but for location and value, I'd happily book again.

The third-floor room looked straight onto the leafy courtyard, not the city skyline, but that turned out to be a blessing--morning light filtered through the maples without any street noise. The wifi held strong even during evening video calls, which surprised me for an older building. Decor-wise, the lobby keeps its classic Art Deco bones, and the guest rooms walk a fine line: the furniture isn't new, but the crisp white linens and fresh paint keep it from feeling tired. I checked in on a Tuesday and left Thursday, and honestly, that second night flew by. I could have easily stayed one more day just to use the pool terrace again. Breakfast was a simple continental spread, but the coffee was excellent. A solid, comfortable pick, and I'd return without hesitation.

We stayed at the Amalfi for a quick two-nighter, and honestly, I could have used one more day just to soak in the atmosphere. The location was a quiet goldmine--steps from the harbor restaurants but tucked away enough that our room felt like a peaceful retreat. I slept like a log both nights; the blackout curtains did serious work, and the bed had that just-right firmness without any of that annoying sag in the middle. The decor leans traditional rather than trend-forward, think warm wood and soft cream tones, but it felt well-maintained and cozy rather than tired. Our only regret was not booking a longer stay to try the pool and breakfast spread. A genuinely comfortable, convenient stop worth repeating.

I was genuinely surprised by how comfortable this stay turned out to be, especially given the hotel's slightly older reputation. The lobby has that classic, polished feel--marble floors and dark wood--and while the guest corridors show a few scuffs, my room itself felt fresh and well-kept, with a crisp white duvet and modern bedside USB ports. Breakfast was a real highlight: the made-to-order omelet station beat any generic buffet, and the fresh pastries were still warm at 7 a.m. I slept like a log on the firm mattress, and the blackout curtains actually did their job despite the bright streetlights below. The wifi was consistently strong--streamed a movie in bed without a single buffering pause. The only tiny disappointment was the pool being chilly, but that didn't dampen an otherwise smooth, efficient, and pleasant two nights. I'd happily book here again for business or a quick city break.

The Conrad exceeded expectations from the moment I walked in. The bathroom was a standout--a massive walk-in rain shower with excellent water pressure, plus thick, plush towels that actually felt spa-quality. As for the decor, it felt refreshingly current, not sterile or tired; the warm wood accents and soft lighting created a genuinely cozy atmosphere. Our room was spotless, with no dust or wear and tear visible anywhere, and the housekeeping team did a meticulous job each day. Breakfast in the restaurant was a lovely surprise: the made-to-order omelets were perfectly fluffy, and the fresh pastries were still warm. Even the coffee was properly strong. Everything felt seamless, calm, and genuinely cared-for. I left feeling rested and impressed, and I'd happily book again without hesitation.

Fairmont Chicago delivers a classic, refined stay rather than cutting-edge style--the lobby's marble and warm wood feel timeless, not tired, and our room's furnishings were well-kept even if the palette leaned traditional. The Wi-Fi was rock solid throughout, easily handling video calls from the desk by the window. Breakfast in the main restaurant was a highlight: the made-to-order omelet bar was quick, and the fresh pastries and strong coffee set us up for a long day of sightseeing. Being steps from Millennium Park and a short walk to the Riverwalk made mornings effortless, and the doormen's transit tips saved us time. Staff were consistently courteous, and the pool was a bonus after a hot afternoon. A dependable, polished choice--I'd book again if returning to the Loop.

From the moment I walked into the lobby with its golden guitars and rock memorabilia, I knew this wasn't going to be your standard cookie-cutter stay. The front desk crew were absolute legends--charming, fast, and genuinely funny, offering tips on the best local taco spots without any of that stiff corporate politeness. My room on the tenth floor was spotless, with crisp white linens and a killer view of the strip, and I never heard a peep from the hallway or neighboring rooms despite the hotel being fully booked. The Wi-Fi was surprisingly solid too; I streamed a movie without a single buffering wheel, which is more than I can say for most places I've crashed. Sure, the pool gets lively and the bar hums at night, but if you're after quiet, the room seals it off beautifully. Solid, rock-and-roll hospitality that actually delivers. I'd come back in a heartbeat.

My corner room on the 24th floor had a sweeping view of the river and the skyline that made me want to linger by the window every evening. The wifi was genuinely dependable, even during peak hours, which meant I could stream a movie without a single drop. Breakfast offered a solid spread, from made-to-order omelets to fresh pastries, though the coffee was just okay. What really stood out was the staff: the front desk remembered my name by the second day, and the housekeeping team left a handwritten note about a local running trail I'd inquired about. I've stayed at pricier properties that made me feel more like a transaction; here, every encounter felt personal and unhurried. A few minor scuffs on the hallway paint and a slow elevator on checkout morning were negligible against the warmth and efficiency of the entire stay. I'd gladly return.

Breakfast at Homewood was a pleasant surprise--hot scrambled eggs, crispy bacon, and fresh waffles that weren't soggy. The bathroom was spotless with a strong shower and plenty of hot water, though the towels could've been plusher. I slept like a log; the mattress was firm but supportive, and the blackout curtains did their job against the morning sun. The Wi‐Fi held up without a single drop, even while streaming a movie on my laptop. Nothing fancy, but everything worked exactly as it should. Staff were friendly at check-in, and the room felt quiet despite being near the elevator. For the price, this was a solid, hassle-free stay--I'd book again without hesitation.

The Hyatt was a solid choice for our anniversary getaway. The bathroom felt like a small spa retreat, with excellent water pressure in the rainfall shower and thick, fluffy towels that actually wrapped around you. I was pleasantly surprised by how quiet our room was, despite the hotel being fully booked; we never heard hallway chatter or street noise. Our corner room faced the river, and watching the city lights flicker at dusk was a real treat. The housekeeping team clearly took pride in their work--the carpet looked vacuumed, the glass surfaces were streak-free, and the sheets smelled fresh without being overpowering. Everything felt crisply maintained, from the bedside lamps to the minibar. It wasn't flashy, but it was exactly what we needed for a restful weekend, and the front desk even surprised us with a small dessert for our anniversary. We'd happily book here again.

I booked two nights but left after one, and honestly, that's the only regret I have about my stay at the InterContinental. I slept like a log in the ridiculously comfortable bed, waking only to the soft glow of sunrise over the river. The staff from the doorman to the housekeeping team were unfailingly gracious, never once making me feel rushed or like a bother. Breakfast in the main dining room was a highlight; the made-to-order omelets were perfect, and the fresh pastries were still warm. Between exploring the city and relaxing in my immaculate room, the time simply evaporated. I'm already plotting a return trip with a proper long weekend, because one night here just isn't nearly enough to soak it all in.

I was honestly prepared for downtown noise, but my room on the eighth floor was remarkably peaceful--just the faint hum of the city below. The staff felt genuinely attentive without hovering, especially the front desk agent who remembered I mentioned an early flight and had coffee ready at 6 a.m. The decor surprised me: sleek and crisp, with warm wood accents that still felt current, not like a hotel stuck in 2015. My corner room faced the river, and watching the lights flicker on the skyscrapers at dusk was a quiet thrill. Bathroom was spotless, rainfall shower had real pressure, and the bed was firm enough to sleep like a rock. A few scuffs on the hallway baseboards, but nothing that dampened the experience. I'd absolutely book again next time I'm in town.

Our corner room at the Knickerbocker was a pleasant surprise. The view stretched from the glittering Magnificent Mile down to the lake, and I found myself just watching the city lights at dusk, which felt like a free show. Given the prime location, I'd say the rate was fair--not a bargain, but you're paying for that postcard scenery and the easy stroll to everything. The front desk crew were genuinely warm, even when we asked for extra towels twice, and the doorman remembered our names by the second day. The bathroom, though compact, had a rainfall shower with strong pressure and fluffy robes that made it feel indulgent. The bed was plush, and the blackout curtains worked perfectly. Only minor hiccup: the elevator wait during checkout rush. Still, I left rested, impressed, and already planning a return.

The Hotel Monaco exceeded expectations in nearly every way. Breakfast was a highlight--the made-to-order omelets were fluffy, and their fresh pastries paired perfectly with strong coffee. Given the prime location and thoughtful touches like the evening wine reception, it absolutely felt worth the splurge. My only regret is that I booked just two nights; I could have easily spent four, unwinding in the cozy yet stylish room. The view over the historic district was charming, especially at dusk when the streetlights flickered on, though rooms facing the courtyard are quieter if you're a light sleeper. Staff were genuinely warm, offering great local dining tips without being pushy. I left refreshed and already planning a return--just a bit longer next time.

I wasn't sure what to expect from a downtown Omni, but this one surprised me in the best way. I slept like a rock--the blackout curtains actually worked, and the bed had that perfect balance of firm and plush. Breakfast downstairs was a cut above the usual hotel buffet; the omelet station was fast, and the fresh pastries were still warm. Honestly, I could have stayed another day just to lounge in the lobby with a coffee, but our schedule was packed. When I checked the bill, I felt the rate was justified, especially given the room size and the quiet despite being near all the action. It wasn't a bargain, but it wasn't a rip-off either. If you're on the fence, book it--just give yourself more time than we did. I left wishing we'd planned an extra night.

The Hotel Palmer was exactly what I needed after a long travel day, and honestly, it felt like a steal for the quality. My room was spotless, from the crisp white linens to the gleaming bathroom fixtures, and the housekeeping had clearly paid attention to every detail. The building itself is wonderfully solid--my room faced the street, but I heard nothing but a faint hum of traffic, which faded completely once I closed the window. I slept like a log on that firm, comfortable mattress; it was the best rest I'd had in weeks. The location is unbeatable, yet somehow the space felt serene and insulated from the bustle outside. For the price I paid, especially given the prime spot and the meticulous upkeep, I'd say it was well worth it. I will definitely be back.

I was a bit wary booking the Sheraton, given its size, but my stay exceeded expectations. The room was surprisingly quiet, with solid soundproofing that let me sleep in despite a full house. The Wi-Fi was fast and stable for both streaming and video calls, which I really appreciated. Decor-wise, it's not cutting-edge, but the classic, warm tones and updated bedding kept it feeling fresh rather than dated. Breakfast was a highlight: a generous buffet with made-to-order omelets, fresh pastries, and decent coffee--definitely above the usual hotel standard. Staff were efficient, and the location made exploring easy. It's not a boutique experience, but for comfort and reliability, I'd happily return.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have picked a better spot. The Sofitel's location was perfect for wandering--right between the river and the main shopping streets, so we never felt stranded. The wifi in the room was solid, even for a couple of late-night work calls, which was a relief. Breakfast was a real highlight: the pastries were flaky and fresh, and they had a nice mix of hot items plus a decent cheese spread, definitely better than your average hotel buffet. Given the quality of the bedding and how quiet the room was, I felt the price was justified--not cheap, but you're paying for that polish. Staff were professional without being stuffy. I'd happily book here again.

Swissotel Chicago turned out to be a genuinely pleasant surprise. The location is unbeatable--steps from the riverwalk and a short stroll to Navy Pier, which made evening exploring effortless. I was half-expecting tired, corporate decor, but the lobby feels crisp and contemporary, with warm wood accents that haven't aged badly at all. The front desk team was exceptionally warm, even helping me rebook a dinner reservation when my plans shifted at the last minute. My room had a lovely lake view, and the bed was so comfortable I nearly missed my morning meeting. If anything, my two nights felt far too brief--I could have easily settled in for a lazy weekend. The only minor quibble is the elevator wait during peak check-in, but that hardly dampened an otherwise flawless stay. I'd absolutely return.

The Hotel Talbott felt like a hidden gem tucked away from the chaos, and I'm already planning my return. From the moment I walked in, the staff were genuinely warm--not the rehearsed friendliness you often get--and they remembered my name the next morning, which was a lovely touch. Breakfast was a quiet, elegant affair with perfectly flaky croissants and a made-to-order omelet that beat any chain buffet. My room overlooked the leafy street, and watching the city lights flicker on from that window was a real treat. The bed was supremely comfortable, with plush pillows that cradled me into a deep sleep--the kind I rarely get at home. Everything felt thoughtfully curated, and while it's not the flashiest spot, its understated charm won me over completely.

I was honestly a bit skeptical booking Affinia on a budget, but it turned out to be a solid value. The bed was the highlight--firm enough for support but with a plush topper that had me sleeping like a log until 9 AM, which never happens on business trips. The room's decor is a mix of clean contemporary and a few quirky touches that feel intentional, not tired, though the hallway carpet shows some wear. I only had one night, and I did wish I could stay another just to use the pool and lounge area; it felt like two days would be perfect. For the price I paid, especially given the location near everything, I'd call it a fair deal. The staff were genuine, and the blackout curtains were a godsend. I'd return without hesitation.

I was a bit nervous booking Hotel Allegro, given the mixed-age reviews, but it genuinely exceeded expectations. The location is unbeatable for exploring the Loop, and honestly, the price felt fair for what you get--the room was spotless, with a surprisingly plush bed and a quiet corner that made me forget I was in the middle of a city. The wifi was flawless; I streamed videos and joined a work call without a single drop. My window faced west, and catching the sunset over the rooftops was a lovely, unplanned perk. Breakfast was the highlight each morning: a solid spread of fresh pastries, made-to-order eggs, and proper coffee, served with no rush. The staff even remembered my room number by day two. Minor wear in the hallway carpet, but nothing that mattered. I'd happily rebook next time I'm in town.

I was a bit skeptical about the WiFi after reading some older comments, but it turned out to be rock-solid--I streamed video and joined a video call without a single drop. The front desk crew genuinely made the stay, though; they remembered my name by the second day and went out of their way to draw a map to a hidden little trattoria that became my favorite meal of the trip. My room was spotless, with that fresh, just-cleaned scent and crisp sheets that made me look forward to crashing each night. The bathroom was compact but thoughtfully arranged, featuring a fantastic rainshower head and fluffy towels that were replaced without me even asking. Everything felt effortless, which is exactly what you want on vacation. I'd happily book here again.

The bathroom was the real highlight for me--a walk-in rainforest shower with excellent water pressure and those big, fluffy towels that actually wrap around you properly. Breakfast had a solid spread: made-to-order omelets, fresh pastries, and a surprisingly good Greek yogurt bar with local honey. My corner room looked straight out over the harbor, and I spent a good hour each morning just watching the ferries glide in, especially at sunrise when the water turned gold. The room itself was spotless, right down to the baseboards and the glass shower door without a single streak. Housekeeping even folded my stray charging cable neatly on the desk. Minor quirks like a slightly squeaky closet door didn't bother me--the staff were so warm and the location unbeatable. I'd happily return, and I'm already checking dates for next spring.

The room's floor-to-ceiling window faced the bay, and I'll admit I spent at least an hour just watching the ferries slide past at dusk--lights flickering on one by one. Wi‐Fi was rock solid throughout, even from the balcony, which surprised me given how many devices I had connected. The bed was the real highlight: firm but plush, and I slept straight through until my alarm, which never happens in hotels. The bathroom mirrored the rest of the space, all cool marble and a rain shower with real pressure; the soaps smelled of cedar and citrus, a nice switch from the usual generic bottles. Staff checked me in quickly and even remembered my coffee order at breakfast the next morning. If you want a dependable, quietly luxurious escape without any fuss, this place earns its name--I'd book again without hesitating.

We booked the Fairmont for a quick anniversary getaway, and I'm genuinely glad we did. The bathroom was a standout--huge marble walk-in shower with excellent water pressure, plus robes that actually fit. Wi-Fi was spotty in the hallway but rock-solid in the room, which mattered since I had to log a few work hours before dinner. Location-wise, you can't beat it; we strolled to the lake, caught a show, and walked back without once needing a cab. If anything, the stay felt too short--I could've happily parked in that bed for another night, but we had to check out and head home. Staff were warm without being fussy. Just wish we'd booked one more day.

Stayed at Hard Rock for a long weekend and honestly came away impressed. The room was spotless--crisp white linens, no stray hairs in the bathroom, and the surfaces actually looked wiped down. Given the prime location and the way the place is styled, I expected to pay a tourist tax, but the rate felt fair for what you got. I'm a light sleeper, yet the blackout curtains and quiet hallway meant I slept through the night both evenings, which never happens for me in hotels. Staff stood out, too. The front desk clerk remembered my name at checkout, and housekeeping proactively restocked the coffee pods without me asking. Minor quibble: the elevator wait got long at peak hours, but that's a small price. I'd book again without hesitation.

My three-night stay at the Hilton was exactly what I needed, and honestly, I could have used a fourth day to fully unwind. The room was spotless, with crisp white linens and a bathroom that gleamed like it had just been sanitized. I was a bit worried about street noise given the central location, but the double-glazed windows kept everything wonderfully hushed; I slept like a log. The highlight was the view--a sweeping panorama of the city skyline that shifted from glittering lights at dusk to soft, hazy gold at sunrise. I never felt rushed, though the time flew by. The housekeeping staff were discreet and efficient, refreshing towels daily without ever intruding. It's rare to find a hotel that balances comfort, quiet, and convenience so seamlessly. I'm already checking dates for my return visit.

Stayed three nights at Homewood and came away genuinely impressed, though I'll admit the lobby made me pause--those dark wood beams and patterned carpet feel a little 2005, not fresh. But my room on the eighth floor flipped that first impression. The view faced the river, and watching the barges ease past during golden hour made the whole trip feel calmer. Bathroom was the real win: a deep soaking tub, excellent water pressure, and towels thick enough to dry off twice. The bed was firm without being board-like, and the blackout curtains actually worked. At $189 a night, I'd call that fair for the size and quiet. Decor could use a refresh, sure, but everything was spotless and functional. I'd return without hesitation.

I was honestly impressed with how smoothly everything went at the Hyatt. The front desk team greeted me by name and even remembered I'd mentioned wanting a quiet floor, which was a thoughtful touch. My room was spotless--no stray hairs in the bathroom, crisp sheets, and the carpet actually looked vacuumed. The view faced the city skyline, and at dusk the lights were genuinely beautiful without feeling touristy. I'll admit I braced for tired furniture, but the space felt recently refreshed: the armchair looked new, and the bedside USB ports were a practical bonus. The hallway carpet showed slight wear, but that's inevitable. Staff in the hallways always smiled, and housekeeping restocked my coffee without me asking. Nothing flashy, just well-executed basics with a touch of care. I'd book here again without hesitation.

Stayed here for a long weekend and was genuinely impressed. The location is unbeatable--we walked to the harbour and the old town in under ten minutes, which made sightseeing effortless. I'll admit I was a little worried the interiors might feel tired, but the lobby and our room struck a nice balance between classic elegance and modern touches; the carpet was spotless and the furniture felt well-maintained. Our corner room offered a sweeping view over the marina, and watching the boats come in at sunset was a real highlight. The Wi-Fi was reliable throughout, which let me catch up on emails without any frustrating drops, and even streaming a film at night worked without buffering. Breakfast had plenty of variety, and the staff were attentive without hovering. Minor quibble: the gym could use a few more free weights, but that's nitpicking. I'd happily return.

The location on the strip can't be beaten, but the real highlight was the unexpected calm. We grabbed a spot by the pool early, and the view of the ocean from the higher floors is genuinely stunning at sunrise. Breakfast each morning was a proper spread--think made-to-order omelets and fresh pastries, not just the standard continental fare. While the lobby has a sleek, modern vibe that feels current, the guest rooms lean a bit more traditional with older carpet; it's not shabby, just noticeably dated. That said, the staff were the true stars. From the front desk who remembered our room number to the bartender who mixed a perfect Old Fashioned, everyone was warm and proactive without being pushy. We left feeling genuinely rested, and that's worth a lot.

After a long travel day, I was frankly dreading a mediocre hotel bed. Instead, I slept like a rock--the mattress was firm but yielding, and the blackout curtains made the room a perfect cave. The cleanliness was impeccable, from the streak-free mirrors to the crisp, fresh-smelling linens. The staff felt genuinely attentive without hovering; the front desk remembered my name and the valet had great local tips. My corner room's view was the real reward, though: a sweeping, glittering panorama of the city skyline at dusk that made me pull up a chair and just sit there. Minor quibble: the shower pressure was slightly weak, but that's a small price for such a peaceful, well-run stay. I'd happily return.

Stayed three nights for a business trip and honestly couldn't have picked a better spot. The location is unreal--steps from the riverfront and a quick walk to all the good restaurants, yet the room was eerily quiet. I slept like a rock through two busy weekdays, which never happens in downtown hotels. My corner room faced the water, and watching the barges glide by at sunset was a peaceful bonus I didn't expect. The staff genuinely stood out--front desk remembered my name on day two and the bartender mixed a perfect old fashioned without me even asking. Check-in was swift, and housekeeping was thorough without being intrusive. Only minor gripe: the hallway carpets felt a bit dated. But the vibe, the calm, and the friendly service make me want to come back for a leisure stay.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded expectations for the rate we booked. The room was spotless, with a bed that made it hard to get up in the morning--those blackout curtains actually work. Bathroom was a highlight: rainfall shower with strong pressure and plenty of hot water, plus the towels were thick and plush, not those scratchy hospital ones. Wi-Fi was surprisingly reliable; I streamed a movie without a single buffering pause. I was worried about street noise, but the double-glazed windows kept everything silent--we heard nothing but the AC hum at night. The location is convenient too, a short walk to tourist spots but far enough to escape the crowds. Sure, the lobby gets busy, but for the comfort level, I'd definitely book again. Worth every penny.

Stayed three nights for a business trip and was genuinely impressed. The room was spotless--fresh linens, no dust on the baseboards, and the housekeeping even folded my loose charger cord neatly. For the rate I paid, it felt like a steal compared to the chain hotels nearby. The bathroom was compact but modern, with a rainfall showerhead that had strong, hot pressure and those thick towels that actually absorb. I slept like a log both nights; the blackout curtains did their job, and the mattress was firm but supportive, no springs poking through. Only minor gripe: hallway noise bled through around 7 a.m. on the last morning. Still, I'd book again without hesitation--clean, quiet enough, and honestly a great value for the location.

Stayed here for a business conference and was pleasantly surprised by the whole experience. The room was spotless, with fresh linens and a carpet that actually looked vacuumed, which is rarer than it should be. The Wi-Fi was fast and reliable--I streamed a video call without a single drop, which made working from the room a breeze. The bathroom had excellent water pressure and the rainfall showerhead was a treat after long days, though the glass door did let a bit of light in early morning. Street noise was minimal thanks to the double-paned windows; I only heard distant sirens twice all week. The bed was firm but comfortable, and housekeeping was prompt each day. Minor quibbles aside, this was a solid, hassle-free stay that met all my needs. I'd happily book again for future trips.

Stayed here for a long weekend and was genuinely impressed. The location is a huge win--we walked to the Louvre and the Seine in under ten minutes, and the metro was practically on the doorstep. The wifi was flawless throughout, even in the hallways, which was a pleasant surprise. Our room faced the inner courtyard, so it was wonderfully quiet, especially at night; I barely heard a peep. The decor felt more classic than cutting-edge, but it was tasteful and well-maintained, with plush carpets and elegant touches that didn't seem tired. The staff were attentive without being fussy. Breakfast was a lovely spread of pastries and fresh fruit. All in all, a very relaxing and convenient base, and I wouldn't hesitate to book here again.

Stayed here for a business trip and was pleasantly surprised by how smoothly everything went. The location is unbeatable--right next to the metro and a short stroll to the waterfront, which made getting around a breeze after my meetings. Wi-Fi was strong and reliable in both the room and the lobby, no dropped connections during video calls, which is rare in my experience. The staff genuinely stood out; from the cheerful front desk who upgraded me to a higher floor to the housekeeper who remembered my late checkout request without being reminded. Considering the service and the comfy bed, I'd say it was worth every penny, even though it's not the cheapest option. Room was quiet, the breakfast buffet had solid variety, and I left feeling refreshed. Would happily book again.

The Hotel Talbot exceeded my expectations, though I wish I'd booked one more night. The staff were the real highlight--from the cheerful doorman who remembered my name to the front desk clerk who patiently mapped out a running route along the river. My room faced the courtyard, which meant a leafy, tranquil view instead of street noise. The decor felt pleasantly vintage, with brass fixtures and floral drapes that seemed intentional rather than tired. It's a charming throwback, not a museum piece. Breakfast was generous, and the evening turn-down service with homemade cookies was a lovely touch. The only reason I'm not giving five stars is the slightly soft mattress, but honestly, given how welcoming everything felt, I'd still return in a heartbeat.

The Affinia turned out to be a genuinely pleasant surprise. The bathroom was a standout--spacious, flawlessly clean, with a rainfall shower that had excellent pressure, plus those lovely little Aesop toiletries that felt like a proper treat. Check-in was swift, and the staff, from the front desk to the bellman, were wonderfully attentive without being overbearing; they even remembered my preference for a high floor without me having to ask twice. My only real complaint is that my two-night stay felt far too short to fully enjoy the cozy, modern room and the cozy lobby bar. For the location and the level of service, I honestly felt the price was fair--not a steal, but certainly worth it for a comfortable, hassle-free city break. I'd happily return.

Stayed three nights at Allegro and left genuinely impressed. The bed was firm but supportive, and the blackout curtains worked wonders--I slept straight through until 8am, which never happens at home. Despite being a few blocks from the main square, the room was remarkably hushed; the double-glazed windows completely muffled the street noise. Breakfast was a pleasant surprise, with a made-to-order omelette station and fresh pastries that beat the usual hotel buffet fare. Location-wise, you couldn't ask for more: a five-minute walk to the cathedral and surrounded by cozy cafes and bakeries for afternoon coffee breaks. The only minor hiccup was the shower pressure fluctuating in the morning, but that's nitpicking. Would absolutely book again for the quiet nights and unbeatable convenience.

Wished we could have stretched our time here into a second night, but even one evening at Hotel Amalfi felt wonderfully complete. The room was spotless, with crisp white linens and a bathroom that gleamed like it had just been sanitized. Breakfast was a pleasant surprise--fresh pastries, creamy cappuccino, and ripe fruit that didn't taste like it came from a can. Location-wise, you couldn't ask for better; we strolled to the marina in under five minutes and stumbled upon a quiet piazza for dinner. The staff even remembered our names at checkout, which added a personal touch. Only regret? Not booking longer. For a quick coastal stop, this place nails the essentials without fuss.

We only stayed one night, which turned out to be our only regret. The room was spotless--not a single speck of dust on the baseboards, and the bathroom smelled of fresh citrus. We slept like rocks on that cloud-like bed, and the blackout curtains meant we woke up naturally, not at the crack of dawn. Breakfast was a pleasant surprise: fluffy scrambled eggs, crispy bacon, and a surprisingly good make-your-own waffle station with real maple syrup. The coffee was strong and hot, exactly what I needed before heading to the airport. Honestly, I've paid twice as much for chain hotels that felt half as nice. The staff even remembered our names at checkout, which was a small touch that felt genuinely thoughtful. We'll definitely book two nights next time.

Really enjoyed our three-night stay at the Conrad. The location can't be beaten, and while the lobby feels a bit corporate-chic, our room was surprisingly fresh with a lovely modern bathroom. Yes, it's pricey, but the service, the stunning skyline view, and the seamless check-in made it feel worth every pound. Breakfast was a highlight--the made-to-order omelettes were superb, and the pastries were still warm. My only tiny gripe is the hallway carpet looks a little tired, but that's minor. The wifi was fast and reliable in the room and even by the pool, which was perfect for streaming a film at night. Would definitely return.

The Fairmont exceeded my expectations in nearly every way. I slept like a log in the incredibly plush bed, with blackout curtains that made the morning feel like midnight until I chose to rise. The bathroom was a marble sanctuary, complete with a rainfall shower that had fantastic pressure and Le Labo toiletries that felt like a real treat. Breakfast in the main restaurant was a highlight--the made-to-order omelets were fluffy and perfect, and the fresh pastries were still warm. While it's undeniably pricey, the level of service, the spotless room, and that serene night's sleep made me feel like I genuinely got what I paid for. I'd happily book again for a special occasion.

We stayed at the Hard Rock for a long weekend celebrating our anniversary, and the whole experience exceeded our hopes. The view from our room, which faced the lagoon, turned out to be a real highlight. Watching the sunsets reflect off the pool area was a subtle, beautiful touch we didn't expect. The room itself was spotless, from the gleaming bathroom to the crisp, white linens; housekeeping clearly takes pride in their work. I slept better than I have in months, honestly. The blackout curtains truly blocked every sliver of light, and the bed was that perfect mix of firm and plush. Every staff member we encountered, from the valet to the baristas, was genuinely warm and helpful without being intrusive. They even left a handwritten note and a small dessert for our anniversary, which felt personal, not manufactured. We'll definitely be back for another escape. The convenience and energy were remarkable.

Checked in Thursday and, honestly, I could have stayed another three days. The bed was that perfect middle ground between cloud-soft and supportive--I slept like I hadn't in months, only waking because the sunrise streamed through the blackout curtains' edges. The hallway was whisper-quiet all night; the only interruption was the faint hum of the AC, which I actually found soothing. The wifi was flawless, streaming a movie on my laptop in bed with zero buffering, which is rare for a hotel this size. My only complaint is that the shower pressure was slightly weak, but the lobby coffee made up for it. It felt like a quick retreat, and I left genuinely refreshed.

We stayed at the Homewood for three nights, and honestly, it delivered far more than I expected for the rate we paid. Our room on the seventh floor had a killer view of the skyline, especially at dusk when the lights started popping on--it felt like a free show every evening. The staff were the real highlight though; from the front desk to housekeeping, everyone seemed genuinely invested in making our stay smooth, even remembering our names by day two. The Wi-Fi was rock solid, too--I ran a few video calls without a single drop, which is rare for a hotel this size. Breakfast was standard but fresh, and the location made it easy to walk to dinner spots. I'd absolutely book again next time I'm in town. Minor nitpick: the hallway carpets looked a bit tired, but that didn't dull an otherwise great stay.

I was a bit wary about the carpet in the hallways, but honestly, the room itself felt fresh and modern, with clean lines and a comfortable, neutral palette. The Wi-Fi was flawless--I streamed a movie without a single hiccup, which is rarer than you'd think. And the bed? I slept like a log, truly. The blackout curtains did their job, and the mattress had that perfect balance of firm and plush. Surprisingly, it was also dead quiet at night; I heard nothing beyond the soft hum of the AC. I will say the bathroom fixtures looked a little dated, but everything was spotless and functional. Overall, a solid, restful stay. For the price, this location is a steal, and I'd happily book again next time I'm in the area.

The view from our 18th-floor room was genuinely spectacular--a sweeping panorama of the city skyline that shifted from glittering night lights to a soft, golden sunrise. We barely wanted to close the curtains. Breakfast downstairs was a cut above the typical hotel buffet: the made-to-order omelets were fluffy, the pastries were still warm, and the fresh-squeezed orange juice was a small luxury I didn't expect. Location-wise, you couldn't ask for more; we walked to the historic district in under ten minutes, and the metro station was basically at the corner. As for sleep, the bed was firm but comfortable, and the blackout shades did their job perfectly--I slept straight through until my alarm, which never happens at home. A few minor quirks with the Wi-Fi speed, but honestly, the stay felt worth every penny.

Stayed at Hotel James for three nights and honestly couldn't have asked for a better base. The location is fantastic for exploring, but what really sold me was the value. For the quality of the room, the amenities, and the service, I felt like I got a steal. Breakfast each morning was a genuine highlight--fresh pastries, proper coffee, and made-to-order eggs that beat any continental buffet I've tried. The room faced the courtyard, so street noise was never an issue, and the blackout curtains were a lifesaver. I slept like a log every single night, which almost never happens in hotels. The bed was firm but supportive, and the pillows were perfect. If you're weighing options, choose this one--you won't regret it. I'm already planning my return trip.

We booked a corner king for our anniversary and were honestly blown away by the view--the Empire State Building was perfectly framed, glowing across the city at night. Morning coffee on the windowsill was a highlight. Breakfast downstairs was a solid, generous spread with good coffee and made-to-order omelets, though nothing wildly gourmet. Our room was exceptionally quiet at night, a real feat given the location, though you could hear faint traffic if you listened. Being a five-minute walk from Bryant Park, the subway, and a handful of excellent bakeries made it ideal for a weekend. Staff were warm and attentive at check-in. We'd absolutely recommend it for a city stay, and it's priced fairly for what you get. Just don't skip the rooftop bar at sunset.

Stayed here for a long weekend and was genuinely impressed. The room was spotless - the kind of clean that makes you want to kick off your shoes immediately. Staff were warm without being fussy, and the front desk actually remembered my name when I asked for extra towels, which felt like a small, thoughtful touch. The decor leans traditional, but it's been kept up so well that it reads as elegant rather than tired - think rich wood, crisp linens, and soft lighting that doesn't scream 'renovation needed.' For the rate I paid, I'd call it a fair deal, especially given the central location and the quiet at night. Breakfast was solid, and the bar had a nice, unhurried vibe. Would happily book again, though I might splurge on a corner room next time for the extra light. A comfortable, dependable choice that doesn't try too hard and gets it right.

We stayed three nights in a king room with a skyline view, and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The lobby's marble and brass could lean a bit traditional, but our room felt crisp and modern--soft linens, USB ports everywhere, and a bathroom that actually had good water pressure. The staff were the real standout: the front desk clerk remembered our anniversary without us mentioning it and sent up a small dessert plate. Our window faced the river, catching the sunset behind the bridges, which made the higher price tag feel justified. Breakfast buffet was pricey, but the omelet station was worth it. Valet was quick each morning, and the gym had brand-new Pelotons. Yes, the hallways are a little worn near the ice machine, but the overall polish and genuine service made it a solid pick for a special trip. I'd book again.

We stayed at the Palmer for a long weekend, and honestly, it exceeded expectations. Our room on the seventh floor faced the garden side, which meant we woke up to a serene canopy of trees instead of the usual city clamor--a truly lovely surprise. The location was a dream for exploring; we walked to the High Line and Chelsea Market in under ten minutes, and grabbing the subway was effortless. I was a bit worried about street noise, but the double-glazed windows worked wonders. I slept like a log each night, the bed was firm yet plush, and the blackout curtains kept the morning light at bay. It's rare to find a hotel this central that feels this peaceful. The staff were friendly without being intrusive, and the lobby's coffee bar became our daily ritual. For a traveler who values both convenience and quiet, this was just right--we'll definitely book again.

I have to admit, I was a little worried the Sheraton would feel dated, but my corner room was spotless and surprisingly modern. The carpet looked fresh, the bathroom grout was pristine, and the blackout curtains worked perfectly. My only real complaint is that I booked a two-night stay and it simply flew by--I could have easily used a third day just to lounge in that ridiculously comfortable bed. Breakfast downstairs was a pleasant surprise, with made-to-order omelets and proper barista coffee, far above the usual hotel buffet mush. Given the location, the lovely pool, and the overall polish, it genuinely felt worth every penny. I left already checking dates for my next visit.

We booked a standard room for a weekend escape and were genuinely impressed by the level of quiet. Despite the hotel being fully booked, we never heard a peep from the corridors or neighboring rooms--the insulation is superb. The Wi-Fi was a pleasant surprise, too; I streamed a movie on my laptop in bed with zero buffering, and my partner's video call in the lounge area was crystal clear. The bathroom was a highlight: a walk-in rain shower with excellent water pressure and those lovely, thick Hermes amenities. The room itself was spotless--fresh linens, not a speck of dust on the surfaces, and the carpet smelled clean, which is rare. We slept like logs and left feeling genuinely rested. Only wish we'd stayed another night.

We stayed at the Swissotel for a long weekend and left genuinely impressed. Breakfast was a standout--the made-to-order omelet station was a nice touch, and the fresh pastries and proper cappuccino made a great start to the day. The lobby and our room felt modern and clean, not at all dated, with sleek wood accents and soft, warm lighting that made it cozy. I slept like a log on the firm-but-comfortable bed, and the blackout curtains were a lifesaver for sleeping in. The wifi was surprisingly solid; I streamed a movie without a single buffer, which is rare for a hotel. The location was perfect for exploring, and the staff were friendly without being overbearing. Only minor gripe: the bathroom could use a bit more counter space. Otherwise, we'd absolutely book again.

The Hotel Talbot exceeded my expectations--it felt like a steal for the location and service. Yes, the lobby decor leans traditional, but the rooms are freshly updated with crisp linens and modern touches that avoid the dated cliche. I slept like a log on the plush king bed, with blackout curtains that actually block the street light. The bathroom was a real highlight: a spotless walk-in rain shower with excellent water pressure and plush towels. It's rare to find that level of polish at this price point. The only minor quibble was the hallway noise in the morning, but it didn't ruin the overall experience. I'd gladly pay again.

We booked the Affinia at a reasonable rate, and frankly, it felt like a steal for what we got. The bathroom was a pleasant surprise--spacious, with excellent water pressure and plenty of fluffy towels, plus a nice rainfall showerhead that made mornings feel luxurious. The wifi was solid the entire stay, no dropped calls during a video conference from the room, which is always a gamble. My only minor caveat is that we could hear hallway chatter now and then, but the room itself was quiet enough, and the bed was so comfortable that I slept like a log anyway. For the location and amenities, I'd absolutely choose this place again. A genuinely smooth, hassle-free experience that exceeded expectations without breaking the bank.

We booked a standard room for a quick weekend getaway, and honestly, the spotless condition of it blew me away. The white linens were crisp, and the bathroom smelled like fresh citrus, which was a lovely touch after a long drive. Our window faced the inner courtyard, so instead of a grand vista, we got a peaceful view of the small fountain and the late afternoon sun hitting the ivy. It was calming, not flashy. The front desk team, especially a gentleman named Marco, was incredibly attentive, even calling up to check if we needed extra pillows after seeing us check in with a toddler. Though we had planned for two nights, the time flew by--we barely had a chance to use the pool. It felt far too short, and we left with that familiar, wistful feeling of wanting just one more lazy morning in the big, soft bed.

We stayed at Hotel Amalfi for four nights and honestly, it exceeded expectations. Our room was spotless, with fresh linens and a bathroom that gleamed--a detail I always appreciate. Despite being near the main road, the double glazing did its job; we slept deeply and undisturbed each night. The staff, especially the front desk gentleman, were wonderfully attentive without hovering, offering excellent local eating suggestions. The location proved ideal, a short, pleasant stroll to the duomo yet removed from the chaos. The breakfast spread was decent, and having a cold bottle of water waiting in the mini-bar was a thoughtful touch. If you value a clean, quiet base that doesn't break the bank, this is a solid pick.

Stayed here for three nights and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The location was perfect--steps from a metro stop and a short stroll to some great local eateries, which made exploring effortless without being in the tourist chaos. Our room faced the inner courtyard, so it was remarkably peaceful; the only sounds were distant morning chatter from the staff, but never disruptive. I was worried about noise given the central spot, but the windows did their job brilliantly. Breakfast was a pleasant surprise, with fresh pastries, made-to-order eggs, and proper coffee rather than the watery stuff you often get. Considering the quality of the bedding, the spotless bathroom, and the genuinely helpful concierge, I felt it was worth every penny--not cheap, but fair for what you receive. I would happily return next time and will recommend it to friends visiting the city.

Our weekend at the Conrad felt far too brief--we were just getting comfortable when checkout arrived.
