The staff, from the valet to the front desk, anticipated our needs with genuine warmth; the concierge even remembered our coffee preference on the second morning. Our room was immaculate, with crisp linens and a sparkling bathroom that smelled faintly of eucalyptus. I'm picky about WiFi, but the connection here was seamless, streaming video without a single drop. The only reason I hesitate to give five stars is that the breakfast buffet, while delicious, ran out of fresh pastries by 9 AM. Still, the housekeeping team refreshed our towels twice daily and left our space spotless. A memorable, cozy escape--I only wish we'd booked one more night.

Stayed here for three nights and honestly left impressed. The location was a dream for exploring--we could walk to the harbor in about ten minutes and grab a cab to the old town without any hassle. Yes, it's pricey, but given the plush bedding, the incredibly quiet room, and the genuinely warm service, I felt the splurge was justified. Breakfast was a highlight: the made-to-order omelets were fluffy, and the fresh pastries and tropical fruit selection felt far above the typical hotel buffet. I slept like a log both nights--the blackout curtains and the soft, supportive mattress were perfect after long walking days. Even the hallway ice machine was silent. If you can manage the cost, this is a solid, comfortable base that won't disappoint.

We stayed three nights over a weekend and, honestly, I was bracing for chaos given the Hard Rock reputation. Instead, it was one of the smoother hotel experiences we've had in a while. The room was spotless--no stray hairs in the bathroom, crisp linens, and the carpet actually smelled fresh. Wi-Fi held up flawlessly for streaming and video calls, which was a pleasant surprise for a property this size. We were on a higher floor facing the pool, and while there was some ambient bass from the bar until about 11 PM, it faded quickly and never disturbed our sleep. Considering the location and the free breakfast buffet, it felt worth every penny--especially compared to nearby options. Staff were genuinely friendly, not robotic. I'd book again without hesitation.

The room was far more stylish than I expected, with a sleek, modern palette that felt fresh rather than the tired beige I've seen in so many other chains. The staff genuinely impressed me--from the cheerful valet who remembered my name to the front desk agent who proactively recommended a quieter floor when she heard I had early meetings. Wi-Fi was rock solid throughout, even during peak evening hours in the lobby bar, which is where I camped out with my laptop. My only real complaint? The stay felt criminally short. I booked two nights for a conference and wished I'd tacked on a third to explore the rooftop pool and that incredible breakfast spread. The bed was so plush I almost missed my alarm, and the blackout curtains worked like a charm. If you're weighing between here and the generic spot across the street, do yourself a favor--choose this one. I left feeling genuinely rested, not just tolerated.

I'm honestly a little reluctant to leave this review because I want to keep this place a secret. We were on the fourth floor facing the courtyard, and I was braced for hallway noise, but it was almost eerily quiet -- I heard nothing after 10 PM. The blackout curtains did their job, and the bed was firm without being hard; I slept a solid eight hours, which never happens in hotels. The room itself was spotless, right down to the baseboards, and the housekeeper had even folded the toilet paper edge into a neat point. As for the view, it was a pleasant patch of green with a fountain, nothing dramatic, but perfect for morning coffee while watching families wander out to the pool. I'll definitely rebook on my next trip.

I was honestly bracing for a lackluster stay given some older photos I'd seen online, but the Hyatt surprised me. Our room faced the courtyard, and the silence was remarkable--I slept through the night without a single hallway squeak or street rumble, which almost never happens for me. The bedding was crisp and the blackout curtains did their job perfectly. While the lobby has a classic, slightly traditional feel, the room itself felt freshly updated with clean lines and modern fixtures, nothing tired or worn. For the rate we paid, especially with the breakfast included, it felt like solid value--not a steal, but fair for the comfort and service. I'd happily book again for a quiet, stress-free weekend.

We stayed at the Intercontinental for a long weekend, and the location was unbeatable--right in the heart of the city, with the metro entrance steps away. I was worried about street noise, but our high-floor room was remarkably quiet; I slept like a log, deeper than I have in months. The bed was plush without being too soft, and blackout curtains did their job perfectly. Housekeeping kept the room spotless, fresh towels appeared twice daily, and the bathroom sparkled. The only minor hiccup was a slow elevator during checkout rush, but that didn't dampen our experience. If you want a serene, convenient, and impeccably clean base, this is it. I'd book again tomorrow without a second thought.

Wish we'd booked a third night -- two just weren't enough to soak up the Hotel James. Our corner room on the eighth floor gave us a sweeping, postcard-perfect view of the harbor lights twinkling at dusk, which made the short commute to the ferry terminal feel almost like a scenic prologue to our day trips. The staff, from the front desk to the housekeeping crew, were genuinely warm, remembering our names by the second morning and even suggesting a hidden tapas spot that became a highlight. Location-wise, you're smack in the middle of everything -- we walked to the old town in ten minutes and grabbed late-night coffee across the street without hassle. The bed was heavenly, the breakfast spread generous. Honestly, the only downside was having to pack up and leave. We'll be back, longer next time, for sure.

We booked the Knickerbocker for a quick anniversary getaway, and honestly, it was over far too soon. The room was spotless--crisp white linens, gleaming bathroom fixtures, and not a speck of dust on the windowsill overlooking the bustling street below. I slept like a log, thanks to the blackout curtains and the surprisingly plush mattress that cradled my back after a long day of walking. The bed was so comfortable I almost wanted to extend our stay, but the weekend flew by. Given the prime location and the attentive staff who remembered our name each morning, it felt worth every penny. My only regret is not booking a third night.

We had a wonderful stay at Hotel Monaco. The room was spotless, with crisp white linens and a smell of fresh lemongrass the moment you walked in. The bathroom felt modern and luxurious, featuring a rainfall shower with excellent water pressure and plenty of fluffy towels. Our window faced the harbor, and watching the boats bob in the morning light was a genuine treat, even with the slight street noise. I was a bit worried the decor might feel old, but it's actually a clever mix of classic charm and updated touches--velvet chairs next to a sleek desk, that sort of thing. It felt thoughtful, not tired. The staff were all smiles, and the location made everything easy. Definitely a place I'd book again.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded expectations for the rate we paid. The location is a major win--you're smack in the middle of everything, with great restaurants and the waterfront just a short, pleasant walk away. I was a bit worried about the decor based on some older photos, but our room felt refreshed and modern, with clean lines and a comfortable, plush bed. We had a corner room facing the city, and the floor-to-ceiling windows gave us a stunning skyline view at sunset, which was a real treat. The staff were friendly without being overbearing, and check-in was a breeze. Considering the prime spot and the quality of the room, it felt like a solid value. We'll definitely book again when we're back in town.

I'll admit I was a little wary about the decor after seeing some older photos online, but honestly the lobby's marble floors and dark wood paneling felt more classic than dated--our room had a subtle retro charm that grew on me. Breakfast was a pleasant surprise: freshly baked croissants, made-to-order omelets, and a fantastic local honey that I piled onto thick-cut sourdough. The view from our fifth-floor window overlooked the treetops and a sliver of the harbor, golden at sunrise, which made morning coffee feel like a small ceremony. Yes, this place isn't cheap, but between the spotless linens, quiet corridors, and genuinely helpful staff who remembered our coffee order by day two, I'd call it fair value. I'd happily return for a weekend treat.

Stayed three nights for a conference and was genuinely impressed. Check-in was seamless, with the front desk staff proactively offering a late checkout when they saw my evening flight, which I appreciated. The lobby and my room felt recently updated--sleek lines, warm woods, no worn carpet or faded drapes. My corner room had a panoramic view of the city skyline, and watching sunset from the floor-to-ceiling window was a real highlight. Room service was prompt, and the bed was exactly the firmness I needed. For the nightly rate, especially given the location and the quality of service, it felt like fair value. Not a luxury palace, but a solid, comfortable stay that exceeded expectations. I'd happily book here again for a work trip.

We stayed three nights for our anniversary, and it was exactly the restful escape we needed. The room facing the inner courtyard was remarkably silent -- we never once heard hallway noise or street traffic, which is rare for a hotel this size. The bathroom was a marble showcase, with a rainfall shower that had fantastic pressure and a deep soaking tub I actually used twice. Every staff member we encountered, from the doorman to housekeeping, greeted us by name after check-in, and the concierge arranged a last-minute dinner reservation at a lovely bistro without any fuss. The decor strikes a nice balance: the public spaces feel grand and freshly updated, while the guest room's classic furnishings have a timeless, elegant charm rather than anything tired. Our only slight quibble was the minibar cost, but that's typical for this tier. We left feeling thoroughly pampered.

Stayed here for three nights and left genuinely impressed. It wasn't cheap, but for the location and quality, I felt it was worth every penny. Our room on the 28th floor offered a stunning panorama of the city skyline, especially at sunset when the windows caught the golden light. The bathroom was a real highlight - spotless, with a powerful rain shower and soft, thick towels that felt luxurious. Despite being in a busy area, the soundproofing was superb; we heard nothing from the street or neighboring rooms, which made for incredibly restful sleep. The bed was firm yet comfortable, and the blackout curtains did their job perfectly. Breakfast was extensive with fresh pastries and made-to-order eggs. Staff were professional and attentive without being intrusive. If you're after a solid, reliable base with great views and silence, this is it. I'd happily return.

We stayed at the Talbott for a long weekend and were pleasantly surprised by how much we got for the rate. The location was a dream--steps from the L and a short stroll to a dozen great restaurants, so we barely needed a rideshare. The bathroom, while compact, had excellent water pressure and plenty of hot water for morning showers. Our room's windows faced the side street, so it was quiet at night, which we appreciated. Wifi was reliable and fast enough for streaming a movie before bed without any buffering. Overall, it felt worth every penny, especially compared to pricier chain hotels nearby. Nothing fancy, but clean, comfortable, and in the heart of everything. I'd happily book again.

I wasn't sure what to expect with Affinia, but it turned out to be exactly the kind of stay that makes you forget you're in a hotel. The room was generous without feeling cavernous, and the bed was so comfortable I actually slept in past my alarm--which never happens when I travel. What really stood out, though, was how proactive the staff were. We mentioned we were heading to a show and they handed us a map with the fastest walking route plus a couple of dinner spots we hadn't considered. The gym had enough equipment to get a proper workout in, and the lobby coffee in the morning was a nice touch for early risers. Location-wise, you're close enough to walk to major sights but tucked away from the constant street noise. Only tiny hiccup was the elevator wait during peak checkout time, but that's a minor blip. I'd happily book here again.

The Hotel Allegro turned out to be a great pick for our long weekend downtown. I'll admit I booked it mostly for the location near the theater district, but the whole experience was a pleasant surprise. The lobby has this old-school, slightly theatrical vibe that's fun without trying too hard, and check-in was quick even with a line forming behind us. Our room wasn't huge, but it was smartly laid out, spotless, and the bed was genuinely comfortable--I slept like a rock. The staff stood out the most; every single person we passed in the hallways or at the front desk offered a smile and a helpful tip. We didn't try the restaurant much beyond a quick breakfast, but what we had was solid. If you're looking for swanky luxury, this isn't it, but for a friendly, clean, and wonderfully central stay, I'd happily return.

Stayed at Hotel Amalfi for four nights and honestly couldn't have asked for a better base. The location is perfect--close enough to walk to the main sights but tucked away on a quiet street, so you actually get decent sleep. Our room faced the courtyard, which was a lovely bonus; you could hear the fountain at night, which was surprisingly calming. The staff were the real highlight, though. Every single person we interacted with, from the front desk to the breakfast team, was genuinely warm and helpful without being overbearing. They pointed us to a tiny trattoria two blocks away that ended up being our favorite meal of the trip. Breakfast was simple but fresh--good coffee, pastries, eggs made to order. The room itself was clean and comfortable, maybe a bit dated in the bathroom, but spotless and the bed was fantastic. Would happily return.

I wasn't expecting much beyond a place to crash, but the Ambassador genuinely surprised me. The lobby has this warm, classic feel without being stuffy, and the front desk clerk actually remembered my name the next morning, which was a nice touch. My room was incredibly quiet--I slept like a log even though I was facing the main street. The bed was firm but comfortable, and the blackout curtains did their job perfectly. Breakfast was included and it wasn't the usual sad continental spread; they had made-to-order omelets and really good coffee. The only minor hiccup was the elevator being slow during the morning rush, but honestly, it gave me time to check my emails. For the price, especially in this neighborhood, I felt like I got way more than I paid for. I'd definitely book here again for a weekend getaway.

Stayed at the Conrad for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The location is perfect for exploring, but the real standout was the service--front desk remembered our names and the concierge booked us a last-minute river cruise without any fuss. Room was quiet, bed was genuinely comfortable, and I appreciated the Nespresso machine and the little touches like complimentary shoe shine service. Breakfast was solid, though a bit pricey; the omelet station made up for it. Only minor gripe was the gym being slightly warm in the morning, but equipment was top-notch. Valet was quick both times. Would happily return for a business trip or another getaway--it's that rare hotel that feels polished without feeling stuffy.

Fairmont is one of those places where everything just works, which sounds simple but is actually rare. The lobby has that grand, old-school elegance without feeling stuffy, and check-in was smooth even though we arrived early. They stored our luggage and texted us the moment our room was ready, which was a nice touch. Our room overlooked the lake, and the bed was genuinely comfortable--not too soft, not too firm. I also have to call out the concierge desk; they booked us a last-minute reservation at a place that was supposedly fully booked, and gave us a walking route that avoided the touristy crowds. The pool area was a bit busy in the afternoon, but it cleared out by evening. Minor gripe: the hallway ice machine on our floor was out of order, but someone brought ice up within ten minutes of us asking. That kind of response makes up for a lot. Already looking forward to coming back.

Stayed at the Hard Rock for a weekend getaway and honestly left impressed. The rock-and-roll vibe is everywhere--guitars on the walls, a killer playlist in the lobby, even the elevator music is curated. Check-in was quick, and the front desk guy hooked us up with a room on a high floor overlooking the strip. The room itself was clean and comfortable, though a bit on the dark side with all the moody decor. The bed was fantastic, and the blackout curtains did their job. We grabbed drinks at the pool bar one afternoon--overpriced, sure, but the vibe made up for it. Location is unbeatable if you want to be in the middle of everything, and the staff consistently went out of their way to help, from valet to housekeeping. Wouldn't hesitate to book again.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have asked for a smoother experience. The front desk team was warm and efficient even with a packed lobby on Friday afternoon--we were in our room within ten minutes. The room itself was spotless, the bed was genuinely comfortable, and I loved that the blackout curtains actually did their job. Location is a huge plus: walked to the riverwalk, the Bean, and several great restaurants without ever needing a rideshare. The breakfast buffet had solid variety, though it does get busy around 9 a.m., so go early if you want a quiet corner. Also appreciated the gym being open 24 hours--managed a quick workout before checkout. Only tiny gripe: the hallway ice machine on our floor was out of order, but the front desk had someone bring up a bucket promptly. Would happily return here for business or a city trip.

Homewood ended up being exactly the kind of stay I didn't know I needed. The room was spotless and quiet, with a kitchenette that actually had decent cookware--I made breakfast twice instead of eating out. The bed was firm but comfortable, and the blackout curtains did their job perfectly. What really stood out, though, was the front desk team. I had a minor billing mix-up and they sorted it in under five minutes, no hassle, plus they remembered my name the next day and asked about my hike. The free evening reception was a nice bonus, and the pool was warm and uncrowded. Parking was easy and right by the entrance. For the price, I genuinely can't complain. I'd happily book here again for a longer trip.

We booked the Hyatt mainly for its location, and honestly, it exceeded every expectation we had. The lobby is grand without feeling stuffy, and the front desk agent noticed it was our anniversary and surprised us with a room on a higher floor. That little touch set the tone. Our room was quiet, spotless, and the bed was genuinely comfortable--not too firm, not too soft. I'm picky about pillows, and I slept like a log all three nights.

The breakfast buffet was pricey but worth it for the made-to-order omelets and fresh pastries. We also used the pool one rainy afternoon, and it was surprisingly uncrowded. The only minor downside was the elevator wait during checkout rush, but two of three cars were running and it wasn't a big deal. If you want a smooth, comfortable stay in the heart of the city, this Hyatt is a safe bet. We'd book again without hesitation.

Our stay at the InterContinental was genuinely fantastic from start to finish. The room was spotless, with a ridiculously comfortable bed and blackout curtains that made sleeping in way too easy. I loved the little touches, like the Nespresso machine and the fact that the bathroom had both a rain shower and a tub. The staff were the real highlight though--everyone from the doorman to the front desk remembered our names and went out of their way to help with dinner reservations and local tips. The location was perfect for walking to everything we wanted to see, and the lobby bar had a great vibe for a nightcap. We even used the pool, which was surprisingly quiet. For the price, it's hard to beat this level of service and polish. Already planning our return.

I'll be honest--I booked the James mainly for the location, but the stay itself ended up being the highlight of my trip. The lobby has this quiet, understated cool that doesn't try too hard, and the front desk team was genuinely warm without being overbearing. My room faced the river, and the floor-to-ceiling windows made the whole space feel twice as big. The bed was firm but plush, and the blackout curtains actually worked. I'm picky about bathrooms, and this one impressed me--huge shower head, good water pressure, and the Kiehl's products were a nice touch. The gym had decent equipment, though it's small. I grabbed a drink at the bar one night, and the bartender remembered my order the next day, which felt like a small, pleasant miracle. For a few nights in the city, this place hit every mark, and I'd happily return for the views alone.

Stayed at the Knickerbocker for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have picked a better spot. The lobby is gorgeous without feeling stuffy--that old-school glamour mixed with a laid-back vibe. Check-in was a breeze, and the guy at the desk even remembered my name the next morning when I asked for coffee directions, which I thought was a nice touch. Room was on the smaller side, but the bed was insanely comfortable and the blackout curtains actually worked, so I slept like a rock. Location is unbeatable for walking to the river or catching an Uber up north. The rooftop bar gets busy, but we snagged a seat at sunset and the view of the city was worth every penny of the overpriced cocktail. Only minor hiccup was the hallway noise one night, but it died down quickly. Would absolutely book here again for a city escape.

I'll be honest--I booked Hotel Monaco mostly for the location, but the stay itself ended up being the highlight of my trip. The room was compact but smartly laid out, with a ridiculously comfortable bed and a window seat I actually used for morning coffee. The staff genuinely seemed to enjoy their jobs, which made check-in and questions feel easy, not transactional. Their restaurant recommendation was spot-on, too. Pet-friendly is a big plus for me, and my dog got more attention than I did. The gym is small but fine for a quick workout. If you're expecting sprawling luxury, this isn't that, but everything was clean, quiet, and thoughtfully done. I'd absolutely stay here again.

The Omni doesn't just put you in the middle of downtown--it puts you in a genuinely comfortable bubble above the chaos. My corner room had a ridiculous view of the lake, and the bed was so good I actually skipped an early meeting just to stay horizontal. The staff never made me feel like a number; the front desk guy remembered my coffee order by day two. I used the pool when it was quiet, and the towels were huge and warm, not those thin afterthoughts you usually get. Breakfast was pricey, but the omelet station was worth the splurge. Only gripe: the hallway ice machine was on the fritz one night. All in all, I left feeling rested, not frazzled--which is exactly what I want from a business trip. I'd gladly book it again.

My stay at Hotel Palmer was exactly what I needed--a comfortable, no-fuss base that made exploring feel effortless. The room wasn't huge, but it was smartly laid out, with a surprisingly plush bed and blackout curtains that actually worked. I slept like a log.

The real standout, though, was the breakfast. Fresh pastries, good coffee, and eggs cooked to order, all served in a bright little nook off the lobby. It beat any chain buffet I've tried. The front desk team also went out of their way to book a last-minute dinner reservation for me when everywhere seemed full.

Sure, the decor is a bit dated, and you'll hear hallway noise now and then. But for the price, the friendly service, and the quiet street location, I'd happily return. It's not flashy, but it's genuinely solid.

I stayed at the Sheraton for a conference last week and left genuinely impressed. The location is unbeatable if you need to be in the heart of the city, but what really stood out was how smoothly everything ran. The front desk staff were warm and efficient, even with a long line at check-in. My room was on a higher floor and surprisingly quiet, with a comfy bed and blackout curtains that actually worked. I'm a light sleeper, so that mattered. The club lounge had a solid breakfast spread, and the espresso machine was a lifesaver each morning. I also used the pool one evening--it was clean and not overcrowded. The only minor hiccup was slow elevator service during peak hours, but it didn't ruin anything. For the price and the level of service, I'd absolutely book here again.

My stay at Sofitel was a masterclass in understated luxury. From the moment I stepped into the soaring, light-filled atrium, the atmosphere felt calm and effortlessly chic. The room itself was a sanctuary--the bed was impossibly comfortable, with crisp linens that made it hard to leave each morning. I particularly loved the deep soaking tub and the rainfall shower; it was the perfect way to unwind after a long day of meetings. The staff, without exception, were gracious and attentive, remembering my name and coffee order by the second day. The location on State Street was ideal, putting me within walking distance of the river and Millennium Park. While the lobby bar can get a bit lively in the evenings, it adds to the energy. I left feeling genuinely rested and spoiled. A truly wonderful, refined experience that I would happily repeat.

Stayed at the Swissotel for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have asked for a smoother visit. The room on the 28th floor had those floor-to-ceiling windows that made the whole city feel like part of the decor--watching the lights come on over the lake at dusk was a highlight every single night. Bed was firm but comfortable, and the blackout curtains actually did their job. Staff were consistently warm, especially the doormen who remembered our names by day two and always had a tip for where to grab a quick bite or skip a line. The indoor pool was a nice escape after long walking days, and the breakfast buffet had enough variety that even our picky eater found something new to enjoy each morning. Location near the river made it easy to get anywhere on foot or via the L. Could've used a bit more drawer space in the room, but that's a minor nit. Would happily book again.

We spent three nights at The Talbott and honestly, it was the perfect home base. The location can't be beat--we walked everywhere, and coming back to that quiet, tucked-away entrance on Delaware felt like a small escape from the street bustle. Our room was on the smaller side, but it was so thoughtfully laid out that it never felt cramped. The bed was exceptionally comfortable, and I slept better than I do at home. The staff genuinely stood out; from the doorman who remembered our names to the front desk team that booked us a last-minute dinner reservation. The little touches, like fresh flowers in the lobby and the cozy bar, gave it that old-world charm without feeling stuffy. We even appreciated the filtered water station on our floor. It's not the fanciest or flashiest, but it's warm, efficient, and incredibly well-run. We wouldn't hesitate to return.

Honestly, I wasn't sure what to expect with the Affinia, but it ended up being the perfect home base for our long weekend. The location is fantastic--we walked to the park, grabbed late-night bites, and never touched the subway once. What really stood out was the front desk crew; they remembered our names by day two and went out of their way to swap our room when street noise got annoying. The room itself was cozy but cleverly laid out, with a comfortable bed and a small kitchenette that saved us a fortune on breakfast. Bathroom was spotless, water pressure was great. I've paid double for hotels with half the charm. A few dated spots here and there, but the vibe was so welcoming that I honestly didn't care. Would absolutely book again.

Absolutely loved my stay at Hotel Allegro. The location is unbeatable--right in the theater district, so we walked everywhere and never touched the car after parking. The lobby has this quirky, artsy vibe that feels more boutique than chain, and the staff genuinely seemed to enjoy their jobs. They upgraded us to a corner room with tall windows and a surprisingly comfy king bed; the pillows were perfect. Yes, the bathroom is small and the walls are a bit thin (we heard the elevator ding all night), but the nightly live jazz in the lounge more than made up for it. The blackout curtains worked wonders, and the in-room coffee was actually decent. For the price and location, this is a solid, character-filled pick--I'd book again in a heartbeat.

We stayed at the Hotel Amalfi for four nights and honestly couldn't have asked for a smoother getaway. The location is ideal--just enough off the main strip to avoid the racket, but a two-minute stroll gets you to the beach and all the little trattorias. What really stood out was the staff; they remembered our names by day two and went out of their way to book a last-minute boat trip when the tour we wanted was sold out. Our room had a small balcony overlooking the lemon groves, and the scent drifting in each morning was pure bliss. The breakfast spread was generous, with fresh pastries and excellent espresso. Sure, the decor leans a bit traditional, but it's spotless and comfortable. We left feeling genuinely rested and a little sad to go--that says it all. Would absolutely return.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, I was impressed by how smooth everything went. The front desk crew was quick and genuinely friendly, not the usual scripted hospitality. Our room overlooked the pool area, which was a nice surprise, and the bed was seriously comfortable--I slept better than I do at home. The little touches like the complimentary coffee station in the lobby and the way they refreshed the room discreetly while we were out made it feel like they actually care. We ate at the on-site restaurant for breakfast one morning, and the avocado toast was solid, though a bit pricey. Location-wise, it's a short walk to a few decent bars and a convenience store, which came in handy. Would happily book here again for another city trip.

The Conrad exceeded my expectations from start to finish. I booked a standard king, and the room was genuinely spacious with a gorgeous view of the river--the floor-to-ceiling windows made the whole space feel even bigger. The bed was incredibly comfortable, and the blackout curtains actually worked, which I can't always say. The staff at the front desk were warm and efficient, and they proactively arranged a late checkout without me even asking. The bathroom had a rain shower and lovely Aesop toiletries, which was a nice touch. We had drinks at the lobby bar one evening, and the cocktails were well made, though pricier than I'd normally go for. The fitness center was compact but had everything I needed. Location-wise, it's a short walk to the riverwalk and plenty of restaurants. I'd happily return.

Our stay at the Fairmont was exactly what we needed after a long travel day. The lobby feels grand without being stuffy, and the check-in process was smooth and welcoming, even with a small line. Our room overlooked the city and was genuinely quiet, which made for an excellent sleep. The bed was plush without being too soft, and the blackout curtains did their job perfectly. I particularly appreciated the little touches--the turn-down service left a small card with the next day's weather, and the bathroom amenities smelled lovely. We had breakfast at the hotel restaurant and the service was attentive but not hovering. The location made walking to most sights easy, though we did use the valet once and it was quick. Overall, a comfortable, polished stay that met all expectations, and we would definitely return.

We had a blast at Hard Rock. The location is killer, right in the middle of everything, and the whole vibe is just fun from the second you walk in--guitars everywhere, music playing in the lobby, you can't help but tap your foot. Check-in was quick, and the lady at the front desk was super friendly, even upgraded us to a higher floor with a nice view. The room itself was clean and modern, with a comfy bed and a cool rock-and-roll theme without feeling cheesy. The pool area was lively but not overcrowded, and the drinks were strong. We ate at the restaurant one night and the burgers were actually really good. Only tiny downside was the hallway noise from other guests, but that's pretty standard for a busy hotel. Overall, a solid, energetic stay and we'd definitely come back.

We wrapped up a conference downtown and decided to stretch the trip into a long weekend at the Hilton. Honestly, the location was the first win--steps from the river walk and maybe ten minutes to Grant Park. But the real surprise was how quiet the room stayed despite the busy streets below. I'm a light sleeper, and I didn't hear a single siren all three nights. The bed was firm in that just-right way, and the blackout curtains actually did their job. Breakfast at the lobby cafe was pricey, so we grabbed pastries elsewhere, but the in-room coffee was drinkable--a bigger compliment than most hotels get. The front desk clerk remembered my name on day two and offered a late checkout without me even asking. Small touches like that make the difference. I'd book here again for work or play.

I wasn't sure what to expect from a hotel that leans so heavily on being 'homey,' but Homewood genuinely pulled it off without feeling kitschy. Our suite was spotless and way more spacious than I anticipated--the kitchenette actually came stocked with real cookware, so we made breakfast a couple of mornings instead of eating out. The bed was comfortable, and I appreciated the blackout curtains because the hallway light was bright. Staff at the front desk remembered our names by day two, which was a nice touch. The free evening reception on weekdays was a pleasant surprise, and the pool area was clean, even if the water was a bit chilly. Only minor hiccup: the AC unit hummed louder than I'd like. Still, for the price and the location near the interstate, we'd happily book again.

Stayed three nights at the Hyatt for a conference, and honestly, it exceeded what I expected from a big downtown property. The lobby feels grand without being stuffy, and check-in was painless--the front desk agent actually remembered my name the next morning, which was a nice touch. My room on the 14th floor had a sweeping view of the river, and the bed was firm but cozy, with blackout curtains that worked too well (I nearly missed my alarm). The gym is well-equipped, though it gets busy around 7 a.m., so go early. I didn't try the restaurant, but the bar made a solid old fashioned. One small gripe: the hallway ice machine was out of order, but a quick call to housekeeping fixed that within ten minutes. Overall, a comfortable, polished stay that made the business trip feel almost like a mini-vacation. I'd gladly book here again.

Stayed here for four nights on a work trip, and honestly, the Intercontinental more than lived up to its name. The lobby is grand without feeling stuffy, and the check-in process was smooth even though we arrived a bit early. They held our bags and texted us the moment the room was ready, which was a nice touch. The room itself was quiet, well-insulated from street noise, and the bed was genuinely comfortable--I slept better here than I do at home most nights. The pool area is worth a visit even if you aren't swimming; it's got that old-school charm that makes you feel like you've stepped back in time. Breakfast buffet was pricey but generous, with made-to-order eggs that weren't overcooked. Staff were consistently friendly, from the valet to the housekeeping team. Would happily book again.

Stayed at Hotel James for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have asked for a better base. The location is fantastic--steps from the park and easy walking to everything we wanted to see, though we also used the bikes they lend out, which was a nice touch. Room was quiet and dark at night, which I always appreciate, and the bed was genuinely comfortable, not just hotel-speak. The coffee in the lobby each morning was a lifesaver before heading out. Staff surprised me most, though--they remembered our names at breakfast and gave spot-on tips for a neighborhood spot we ended up loving. Valet was quick every time, even on Saturday night. Minor nitpick: the shower pressure could be stronger, but that's about it. Already planning a return.

We chose the Hotel Knickerbocker for a mix of sightseeing and a little R&R, and it hit the right notes. Our room on the ninth floor was surprisingly quiet given the hustle below, and the blackout curtains were a lifesaver after long days. I really appreciated the little things: a proper coffee maker, not one of those pod machines, and a bathroom with excellent water pressure. The location was unbeatable for wandering to Navy Pier or hopping on the L. We didn't eat at the restaurant, but the bar's old-school vibe was perfect for a nightcap. Staff at the front desk were friendly and quick to help with directions. Sure, the decor leans toward classic, and the carpets could use a refresh, but it felt clean and well-cared-for. I'd absolutely stay here again for the blend of history and convenience. The complimentary bottle of wine upon arrival was a pleasant, unexpected touch that set the tone for our whole weekend.

My stay at Hotel Monaco was exactly what I needed--stylish without being stuffy, and located just steps from everything I wanted to do. The check-in was quick, and the front desk clerk genuinely took time to mark up a map with her favorite local spots, which I appreciated way more than the usual scripted suggestions. The room itself was comfortable, with a surprisingly cozy bed and a bathroom that had plenty of hot water and counter space. I also liked the little extras, like the yoga mat and the complimentary wine hour in the lobby--it was a nice way to unwind after a long day of walking. The only tiny hiccup was the street noise at night, but it wasn't enough to ruin my sleep. All in all, I'd happily book here again for a weekend getaway.

We booked the Omni almost on a whim for a long weekend, and honestly, it turned out to be the best decision of the trip. The location is unbeatable--steps from the Mag Mile but quiet enough that we slept like logs. What really impressed me was the check-in process; the front desk agent remembered my name and even had a list of local coffee spots ready when I mentioned we were jet-lagged. The room itself was huge for downtown, with a couch area that meant we weren't tripping over our suitcases. The pool was warm, the gym had actual squat racks, and the housekeeping staff folded my stray charging cable into a neat coil. Only minor gripe: the elevator wait during checkout rush. But honestly, we're already planning our return in the fall.

We booked the Hotel Palmer on a bit of a whim for a long weekend, and honestly, it turned out to be the perfect home base. The location is fantastic--you can walk to so many places, and the train station is right there, which made exploring effortless. The staff were genuinely friendly, from the doorman who remembered our name to the front desk helping us map out a rainy-day itinerary on their tablet. Our room was quiet, which was a blessing, and the bed was incredibly comfortable with soft, high-quality sheets. The blackout curtains actually worked, and we slept in later than we have in months. The little touches, like a proper Nespresso machine and a handwritten welcome note, didn't go unnoticed. We didn't try the restaurant, but the bar made a mean old fashioned. We left feeling rested and would absolutely book again for a city trip.

Stayed at the Sheraton for a conference and honestly, it exceeded what I expected from a big chain. Check-in was a breeze, even with a long line, because the front desk moved people through with real efficiency. My room on the 14th floor was quiet, which is rare, and the bed was genuinely comfortable--I slept like a rock. The bathroom was spotless and the water pressure in the shower was fantastic after a long travel day. I grabbed dinner at the hotel bar and the service was attentive without hovering, and the food was surprisingly good for hotel fare. Location wise, it's central enough to walk to a few good spots, and the staff gave me solid recommendations. The gym was decent, with working treadmills and free weights, nothing fancy but functional. Only minor hiccup was slow Wi-Fi in the evening, but morning speed was fine. I'd gladly book here again for a business trip or a weekend getaway.

I wasn't sure what to expect with a French luxury brand in the middle of downtown, but Sofitel exceeded every expectation. The room was beautifully quiet, which is rare in this part of the city, and the blackout curtains actually worked, so I slept like a rock. The bed was firm yet plush, with linens that felt crisp and cool. What really stood out was the staff--from the valet who remembered my name every single morning to the front desk agent who helped me rebook a flight without any hesitation. The pool is small but never crowded, and the gym had everything I needed. Breakfast was pricey, but the pastries were legitimately fresh and flaky. I'd absolutely stay here again for the service alone.

Really impressed with Swissotel. The location is fantastic--you're steps from the lake and a quick walk to all the main sights, yet the rooms feel surprisingly quiet. We booked a corner room and the views over the water were stunning, especially at sunrise. The bed was incredibly comfortable, and I appreciated the blackout curtains after a long flight. Staff were professional without being stuffy; the front desk remembered my name every time we passed, which was a nice touch. Breakfast had a solid spread with fresh pastries and made-to-order eggs, though it got busy around 9. The pool area is small but clean and never overcrowded. Only minor gripe was the hallway carpet showing some wear, but it didn't detract from the stay. Would happily return.

My stay at Hotel Talbott was exactly what I needed--charming without trying too hard. The building has that old-school character you don't find in chain hotels, with creaky floors and a cozy lobby that smells faintly of wood polish. I booked a standard king, but the room felt generous, with a window seat overlooking the quiet side street and a bed I actually sank into. The front desk clerk remembered my name when I asked for extra towels, which was a small touch that went a long way. Breakfast was simple--pastries, fruit, decent coffee--but served in a sunlit nook that felt more like a friend's dining room than a hotel. Location-wise, it's a short walk to the river and a bunch of good restaurants, though the walls are a bit thin; I heard my neighbor's TV one night, but it faded by 10. All in all, a warm, unpretentious place I'd happily return to.

I stayed at Affinia for a long weekend and honestly came away pleasantly surprised. The location is a massive win--you're right in the middle of everything, yet the rooms stay quiet enough for a solid sleep. I had a kitchenette, which I wasn't expecting, and it came in handy for breakfasts before heading out. The bed was firm but comfy, and the blackout curtains actually worked. Staff at the front desk were friendly without being overbearing, and they let me leave my bags after checkout without any fuss. The gym was small but had what I needed--free weights and a few machines. Wi-Fi held up fine for streaming. It's not fancy, but everything felt clean and well-maintained. I'd definitely book here again for the value and convenience.

Absolutely loved my stay at Hotel Allegro. The location is unbeatable--steps from the theater district and a quick walk to the Loop, yet the rooms are surprisingly quiet. I was a little worried the historic building might feel dated, but the mix of vintage charm and modern updates is spot on. My king room was cozy but well laid out, with a plush bed and excellent blackout curtains that made sleeping in a breeze. The staff genuinely stood out: the front desk remembered my name by my second morning and even texted me a dinner reservation suggestion that turned out to be fantastic. Housekeeping was thorough without being intrusive. The lobby bar has a great buzz in the evenings, and the breakfast service was efficient, though nothing extraordinary. For the price, especially on a weekend rate, this is a steal. I'd happily return and already recommended it to colleagues visiting for shows.

Our room overlooked the little piazza, and honestly, I could have sat on that tiny balcony all day just watching the sea and the lemon trees. The Hotel Amalfi is tucked into the hillside so perfectly that you feel like part of the town itself. Breakfast was simple but plentiful--fresh pastries, local cheese, and the best cappuccino we had on the whole coast. The staff remembered our names by the second morning and helped us book a boat tour that ended up being the highlight of our trip. The room itself was compact but spotless, with a lovely tiled bathroom. The only minor downside was the walk back up from the beach, but the view from the rooftop terrace more than made up for it. A genuinely charming, welcoming place.

Stayed three nights here and honestly couldn't have asked for a smoother trip. The lobby is elegant without being stuffy, and the front desk agent remembered my name each time I walked by--a small touch that made the stay feel personal. Room was spotless and quiet, with a bed that had me sleeping better than I do at home. The blackout curtains actually worked, and the bathroom had great water pressure plus those thick towels you only seem to get at nicer places. Location was perfect for walking to dinner and catching a show, but I also appreciated the hotel bar for a nightcap. The bartender mixed a solid Old Fashioned and chatted without hovering. Only minor gripe: the elevator took a while during checkout rush. Would book again without hesitation.

I'll be honest--I booked the Conrad mostly for its location, but the stay turned out to be the highlight of the trip. The lobby feels understated and classy without trying too hard, and the check-in was smooth even though we arrived early. They stored our bags, texted us the moment the room was ready, and even added a small welcome note for our anniversary. The room itself was quiet, which I never take for granted in a city hotel, and the bed was genuinely comfortable. Breakfast was a bit pricey, but the coffee was excellent and the staff remembered our order on the second morning. The gym is compact but has everything you need. We didn't use the pool, but the view from the lounge at sunset was worth it alone. I'd happily stay here again.

The Fairmont turned out to be exactly what I needed after a messy travel day. Check-in was smooth and the front desk agent noticed my exhaustion and offered a late checkout without me even asking--that little gesture set the tone. The room itself was classic and quiet, with a genuinely comfortable bed and blackout curtains that worked. I slept like a log. The lobby feels grand without being stuffy, and the location is perfect for wandering down to the waterfront or grabbing a cab. I had breakfast at the restaurant one morning and the eggs benedict was properly done, not the usual hotel mush. Housekeeping was unobtrusive and thorough. My only minor gripe is that the hallway ice machine was out of order, but that's a blip. I'd happily book here again for a city stay.

Stayed at the Hard Rock over a long weekend and honestly didn't want to leave. The whole vibe hits you the moment you walk in--music playing, guitars on the walls, just a cool energy without feeling gimmicky. Room was quiet, bed super comfy, and the blackout curtains actually worked, which is rare. I loved that they had a real record player in the room with a small vinyl collection; that was a fun touch we didn't expect. Staff were down-to-earth and quick with dinner spots that weren't tourist traps. Pool area gets busy but the service there kept things flowing. Only minor gripe was the elevator wait during checkout, but that's it. We've already booked our next stay. Solid pick for a fun, comfortable trip.

Stayed at the Hilton for a conference and honestly came away impressed. Location is unbeatable--walkable to everything, and the staff from bellmen to front desk were genuinely friendly without being over the top. Room was spotless, bed comfy, and the blackout curtains actually worked, which is rare. The executive lounge had a solid breakfast spread and the evening snacks were a nice perk after long days. Only minor hiccup was the elevator wait during checkout rush, but that's about it. The gym could use more free weights, but cardio machines were plentiful and new. Pool area got busy around noon but that's expected. Overall, a solid, dependable stay that made the trip easy. I'd book here again without hesitation.

We picked Homewood because we needed a kitchen for a week-long stay, and honestly, it exceeded what we expected. The suite was genuinely spacious--our two kids had their own sleeping nook, and the full-size fridge meant we actually cooked dinner three nights instead of eating out. Breakfast had real variety, not just the sad scrambled eggs you see at some places; the oatmeal bar and make-your-own waffles were a hit. The pool was warm and clean, though it's on the smaller side, so we went at off-hours. Staff at the front desk remembered our room number by day two, which felt personal. Only minor gripe: the hallway ice machine was on our floor but out of order, and they directed us to the next floor. Not a big deal. For the price, especially with the included evening social on weekdays, this is a solid, comfortable pick for families or anyone wanting more than a basic hotel room. We've already booked our next stay.

The Hyatt was exactly what I needed after a long travel day. Check-in was smooth, and the front desk actually remembered my name the next morning, which was a nice touch. My room had a fantastic view of the skyline, and the bed was the kind that makes you want to skip your morning plans just to stay in it. The shower pressure was perfect, and the blackout curtains worked wonders for jet lag. I visited the restaurant for breakfast, and the avocado toast with poached eggs was surprisingly good, not your typical hotel fare. The gym was well-equipped, and the pool area was quiet even on a weekend. Location-wise, it was easy to walk to the waterfront, and the staff gave me a great tip for a less touristy dinner spot nearby. I really have no complaints. It's a solid, comfortable place that got everything right, and I wouldn't hesitate to book it again next time I'm in town.

We booked a club room for our anniversary weekend and the welcome amenity (a lovely prosecco and chocolate-covered strawberries) was a thoughtful touch. The room itself was spotless, with a super comfortable king bed and the blackout curtains really did their job. The gym is top-notch for a hotel, and I actually got a solid workout in before we hit the pool. Speaking of which, the pool area is a bit compact, but we snagged loungers in the morning without issue. Club lounge breakfast was the highlight--the made-to-order omelets and fresh pastries were fantastic, and the staff there remembered our names by day two. Sure, valet parking is steep, but for this level of service and comfort, we'd return without hesitation. A solid five stars for a consistently excellent stay.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have picked a better spot. The lobby has this warm, moody vibe that immediately felt like a escape from the city noise, even though you're right in the middle of everything. Our room was on the quieter side, which was a pleasant surprise--the blackout curtains actually worked, and the bed was that perfect level of firm with soft sheets. I'm still thinking about the breakfast spread; the fresh pastries and made-to-order omelets were a step above typical hotel fare. The staff genuinely seemed happy to help, from the doorman who remembered our name to the front desk arranging a last-minute spa slot. Only tiny hiccup was the elevator wait during checkout rush, but that's hardly worth complaining about. Great value for the location and vibe--I'd definitely book again.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, the location is unbeatable--steps from the Magnificent Mile but tucked away enough to feel like an escape. The room was on the smaller side, but the floor-to-ceiling windows made up for it with killer city views, especially at sunset. I loved the vintage vibe in the lobby; it's got that old-school Chicago charm without feeling stuffy. The staff were genuinely warm, not that fake hospitality energy. Someone at the front desk recommended a deep-dish spot two blocks over that was incredible. The bar upstairs was a nice bonus for a nightcap, though drinks were pricey. Bed was plush, blackout curtains worked perfectly. Only minor gripe--hallway noise carried a bit, but it quieted down early. Would definitely book again for the charm and convenience.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The location is unbeatable--steps from all the action but the rooms are surprisingly quiet, so you get the best of both worlds. Loved the quirky, colorful decor; it's not your typical boring chain hotel. The staff were genuinely friendly, especially the bartender in the lobby who recommended a great local spot for brunch. My room was spotless, bed super comfy, and the blackout curtains worked wonders. Only tiny hiccup was the elevator wait Saturday morning, but it cleared up fast. Would absolutely book again for a city escape.

Stayed here for a long weekend celebrating our anniversary, and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The location is unbeatable - we walked to the waterfront every evening and it was so easy to hop on the T for exploring. The room itself was spotless and quiet, which we really appreciated after some noisy hotel experiences elsewhere. The bed was ridiculously comfortable, and the blackout curtains were a lifesaver for sleeping in. We had drinks at the rooftop bar one night, and the views over the city were stunning, though the cocktails were a bit pricey. The staff genuinely stood out though - from the warm welcome at check-in to the front desk helping us print last-minute concert tickets. Breakfast buffet was solid with made-to-order omelets. Only tiny gripe: the valet was a little slow on Sunday morning, but they were friendly about it. Would absolutely book again for a city stay.

We stayed at the Palmer for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded every expectation we had. The location is perfect for exploring the city, but what truly set it apart was the staff--from the doorman who remembered our names to the front desk team who helped us snag a last-minute dinner reservation. Our room faced the garden, which was a quiet oasis after busy days of sightseeing. The bed was wonderfully firm, and the blackout curtains were a lifesaver. We had breakfast included, and the spread was fantastic, with fresh pastries and made-to-order eggs. The only tiny hiccup was a slow drain in the shower, but maintenance fixed it within the hour of us mentioning it. We left feeling genuinely rested and well-cared for. It's rare to find a hotel that balances classic elegance with such modern comfort. We'll definitely be back.

Absolutely loved my stay at the Sheraton! The moment we walked into the lobby, the staff greeted us with such warmth, even offering a late checkout before we asked. Our room was spotless and the bed? Honestly, I've never slept so well in a hotel. The blackout curtains were a lifesaver after a long travel day. I have to give a shoutout to the bar staff--they made the best Old Fashioned I've had in ages, and the bartender remembered my name on the second night. The pool was a bit busy during peak hours, so we went early morning and had it almost to ourselves. Only tiny hiccup was the elevator wait on floor 14 during breakfast rush, but that's a minor thing when everything else was this polished. Will definitely be back for our next city break, and I've already recommended it to my colleagues. Top notch.

From the moment we pulled up, the doorman's warm greeting set the tone. Check-in was swift, and the room--a Prestige suite--was absolutely spotless. The bed felt like a cloud, and the blackout curtains worked wonders for jet lag. We grabbed cocktails at the bar each evening; the mixologist actually remembered our order on the second night, which was a lovely touch. Breakfast had plenty of variety, though the coffee could be stronger. The only hiccup was a slightly noisy AC unit that hummed all night, but honestly, it faded into background noise. Location-wise, you're steps from the river and a short stroll to the Louvre. Staff went out of their way to print our museum tickets and even recommended a hidden bistro that became our favorite meal of the trip. If you want understated luxury without any snobbery, this is it. We're already eyeing a return visit in the fall.

I picked this hotel mainly for the location, and it didn't disappoint. Being right by the harbour made exploring the city on foot effortless, and the train station was a quick stroll away. The check-in was efficient, though I did have to wait a few minutes for a room to be ready, which was fine. My room had a fantastic view of the water, and the bed was incredibly comfortable - I slept like a log. The breakfast spread was substantial, with a great mix of local pastries and hot items. The only slight downside was the air conditioning being a bit noisy, but it wasn't a dealbreaker. Overall, a very solid, comfortable stay that I'd happily book again.

We loved our stay at the Talbott. The location is just perfect for exploring the Magnificent Mile, but what really sold us was the old-school charm--the lobby feels like stepping back into a more elegant era, without being stuffy. Our room was on the smaller side, but it was spotless and the bed was ridiculously comfortable after long walking days. The staff at the front desk were genuinely warm, remembered our names, and gave fantastic dinner recommendations. The complimentary coffee in the morning was a nice touch, though I wish the hours were a bit longer. The bathroom was tight, but the rainfall shower pressure was great. It's not a flashy modern high-rise, but if you appreciate polished, boutique-style service and a classic Chicago vibe, book here. We'd absolutely return.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have picked a better spot. The staff at the front desk were super welcoming, even let us check in a couple hours early after a red-eye. Room was on the smaller side but immaculate, with a super comfy bed and blackout curtains that actually worked--slept like a rock. The mini-fridge and microwave were a lifesaver for late-night snacks. Location is the real winner, though: a quick walk to the Metro and tons of great food spots around Logan Circle. We did have a minor issue with the key card not working once, but they fixed it in under five minutes with an apology. Would absolutely book again for the value and convenience.

Stayed three nights for a conference and was genuinely impressed. The location is perfect, tucked a block from the river but still close to the old town's busy lanes. My room on the sixth floor had a small balcony overlooking the rooftops--quiet in the morning, just the church bells. The bed was firm but comfortable, and the blackout curtains actually worked, which is rare.

Breakfast was the real highlight: fresh pastries, proper cappuccinos made to order, and scrambled eggs that weren't rubbery. The staff remembered my name by the second day, which felt thoughtful, not forced. Only minor gripe--the gym is tiny with just two treadmills, and the elevator can be slow during check-out rush. But the rooftop bar at sunset made up for it entirely. Would happily return for a leisure stay.

We had a wonderful four-night stay at Hotel Amalfi in early September. The location was ideal, tucked on a quiet side street yet just a two-minute stroll to the bustling promenade and beach. Our sea-view room was spotless, with a comfortable bed and a balcony perfect for watching the sunset with a glass of local wine. The staff truly made the difference--everyone from the front desk to the breakfast servers was genuinely warm and helpful, offering great tips for avoiding the crowds. The breakfast spread was ample, with fresh pastries and excellent cappuccino. While the rooms are a bit dated and the walls slightly thin, we slept well. Overall, it offered fantastic value for the area. We would happily return.

Honestly, I almost didn't book here because of a mix-up with my dates, but the front desk agent, Marco, sorted everything out in minutes with a smile. That set the tone for the whole stay. The room was spotless, the bed was like sleeping on a cloud, and the blackout curtains actually worked. I loved that the mini-fridge had real glassware, not just plastic cups. The location is perfect for exploring on foot, but the best part was the quiet courtyard for morning coffee. Breakfast had fresh pastries and made-to-order eggs, which was a pleasant surprise. The only tiny hiccup was the elevator being slow during peak checkout time, but honestly, it gave me a moment to breathe. I left feeling genuinely rested, which is rare for a business trip. Definitely my new home base in the city.

Stayed for a long weekend and honestly couldn't fault it. The room was spotless, with a ridiculously comfortable bed and a view that made me just sit and stare for an hour. Staff were attentive without hovering--the concierge remembered my name after one interaction and gave great dinner tips. Breakfast buffet had everything, though the eggs benedict was the standout. Pool area was calm even on a busy Saturday, and the loungers were actually spaced out, which never happens. Minor hiccup with the Wi-Fi in the room, but they sorted it within minutes. Location is perfect if you want to be close to the river but away from the tourist crush. Would happily book again, and I'm picky about hotels. Great value for what you get.

The Fairmont definitely knows how to make you feel like you've escaped the everyday. From the moment the doorman greeted us with a genuine smile, the service was attentive without ever being stuffy. Our room had a stunning view of the city skyline, and the bed was so plush I actually looked forward to waking up just to lounge in it. The bathroom was spotless, with thick towels and that lovely Le Labo toiletries scent that lingers nicely. We had breakfast at the main restaurant, and the eggs benedict were perfectly poached, though I'll admit the coffee took a second cup to hit the spot. The pool area was a bit busy on Saturday afternoon, but we found a quiet corner by the cabanas. Check-out was a breeze with the mobile key. A few minor scuffs on the hallway wallpaper, but honestly, it added to the old-world charm. We left feeling rested and a little spoiled. Worth the splurge.

We had a really great stay here for our anniversary. The staff genuinely seemed to care and made us feel special -- the front desk even remembered our reason for visiting and sent up a small dessert plate. The room was clean and quiet, with a super comfortable bed and blackout curtains that actually worked, which is rare. We loved the lazy river and pool area, even on a busy Saturday afternoon. Service at the pool bar was quick, and the cocktails were strong. Drinks at the lobby bar one night were a bit pricey, but that's expected. The location is unbeatable for the Boulevard, and we walked everywhere. Would definitely book again for a fun, easy getaway.

We had a fantastic stay at the Hilton. The location was perfect for exploring, and the staff truly went above and beyond. From the moment we checked in, everyone was incredibly welcoming, and they even arranged a late checkout without us having to ask. The room was spotless and the bed was wonderfully comfortable; I haven't slept that well in ages. We also loved the breakfast buffet--tons of fresh options, and the coffee was actually good, which is rare in hotels.

The only minor hiccup was the pool being a bit busy on Saturday afternoon, but that's not really on them. Overall, it was a seamless, relaxing experience, and we wouldn't hesitate to book here again. A big thank you to the front desk team for making our anniversary feel so special! Highly recommended for both couples and families.

I'm genuinely impressed with how comfortable our stay was at Homewood. The room was spotless and the bed was honestly one of the best I've slept in at a hotel in a long time--firm but not hard, great pillows. The kitchenette came in handy for late-night snacks, and the mini-fridge kept our drinks properly cold. Breakfast had a solid rotation: made-to-order omelets one morning and decent waffles the next. The staff at the front desk were friendly without being overbearing, and they even gave us a great recommendation for a local taco spot that was packed with residents. The only minor hiccup was the elevator being slow at peak checkout time, but it didn't ruin anything. We'll definitely book here again when we're in the area.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have picked a better spot. The location is perfect--right by the waterfront, and everything we wanted to see was a short walk or quick cab away. Check-in was smooth, and they even let us into our room early, which was a huge win after a red-eye. The room itself was spotless, with a super comfortable bed and a great view of the harbor. The blackout curtains were a lifesaver for sleeping in. We hit the pool one afternoon, and it was surprisingly quiet and well-maintained. Only tiny hiccup was the hallway noise on Saturday night, but it died down quickly. The breakfast spread had plenty of options, and the staff were all genuinely friendly, from the valets to the front desk. Would absolutely book here again for a city escape.

Stayed for three nights for a work conference and honestly, the location was the main pull--right by the harbor, a quick stroll to the ferry and some fantastic seafood spots. The room itself was on the higher floors and had a sweeping view that made the morning coffee feel special. Bed was firm but incredibly comfortable, and blackout curtains actually did their job. The bathroom was spotless with great water pressure, which is a win in my book. 

The only hiccup was the Wi-Fi dropping a couple of times during a video call, though it was fine afterwards. Staff at the front desk were efficient and friendly, especially when I asked for restaurant recommendations. The club lounge was a nice perk for evening snacks, though a bit crowded. Would definitely book here again for the convenience and overall comfort. Nothing flashy, but everything done right.

We had a fantastic long weekend at Hotel James. The location is perfect for exploring the city, but the real highlight was the incredible staff. Everyone from the front desk to the housekeeping team was genuinely friendly and went above and beyond. Our room was a quiet retreat from the busy streets, featuring a wonderfully comfortable bed and a large, bright bathroom. The rainfall shower was a particular luxury. I also appreciated the thoughtful touches, like the complimentary coffee in the lobby each morning that was actually good. The on-site restaurant served a delicious dinner, though it is a bit on the pricey side. We left feeling rested and thoroughly impressed. We are already planning our next visit and wouldn't consider staying anywhere else. Highly recommended for a chic and comfortable base.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, the location can't be beat--right in the thick of the Loop, steps from the river walk and a million transit options. The lobby is a stunner, all old-school grandeur with a modern twist, and check-in was painless. Our room was on the quieter side, which was a relief, and the bed was seriously comfortable. The blackout curtains did their job, and the bathroom was spotless, though the shower pressure was just okay. We grabbed drinks at the rooftop bar one night; the views of the city skyline were worth the slightly steep prices. Staff were friendly and quick with recommendations for dinner spots. Only minor gripe: the hallway was a bit noisy early morning, but it didn't ruin anything. Would absolutely book again for the convenience and comfort.

Stayed three nights for a work conference and honestly, the Hotel Monaco was the best part of the trip. The location is perfect--steps from the French Quarter but quiet enough that you actually sleep. My room had this great little balcony overlooking the courtyard, and the bed was absurdly comfortable. I'm picky about pillows, and these were just right.

What really stood out was the staff. From the valet who remembered my name every morning to the front desk clerk who printed my boarding pass without me even asking, everyone seemed genuinely happy to help. The evening wine hour in the lobby is a nice touch too--met some fellow travelers and actually chatted instead of staring at my phone.

Only minor gripe: the bathroom sink drained a bit slowly. But honestly, I'd book again in a heartbeat. That rooftop hot tub at sunset? Worth it alone. Great value for the vibe.

We had a really lovely stay here. Check-in was quick, and the front desk agent was genuinely friendly, not just reciting a script. Our room on the 14th floor had a fantastic view of the park, and I'll admit we spent an embarrassing amount of time just watching the city lights at night. The bed was super comfortable, with great pillows, and the blackout curtains actually worked--a rare find. We grabbed breakfast at the restaurant one morning, and the avocado toast was surprisingly good, though the coffee took a while to arrive. The gym is solid, with new treadmills and plenty of towels. My only minor gripe: the hallway ice machine on our floor was out of order, but a quick call brought a bucket right up. Overall, a very polished, comfortable experience. We'd definitely book here again.

We stayed at The Palmer for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded every expectation we had. The location is perfect, tucked away on a quiet street but just a five-minute walk to the harbor and all the best restaurants. Our room was spotless, with a incredibly comfortable bed and a balcony that caught the morning sun beautifully. The staff were the real highlight though--from the cheerful valet who remembered our names to the front desk team that helped us snag a last-minute reservation at a fully booked seafood place. The rooftop bar is a must for sunset drinks, and the cocktails are actually well-poured. Only tiny complaint was the shower pressure was a bit weak, but everything else was so polished it didn't matter. We've already started looking at dates to come back in the fall. Highly recommend this gem to anyone wanting a relaxed, upscale stay without the stuffy vibe.

We stayed at the Sheraton for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded my expectations. The check-in process was smooth, and the front desk agent actually acknowledged our status tier and upgraded us to a room facing the city, which was a lovely surprise. The room itself was spotless and the bed was, as expected, incredibly comfortable--I slept better there than I do at home. The location was great for walking to restaurants and the water.

The only minor hiccup was the pool area being a bit crowded on Saturday afternoon, but we just went back in the morning and had it almost to ourselves. The lobby bar had a great vibe too, perfect for winding down with a craft cocktail. The staff throughout the hotel were consistently polite and helpful. All in all, a really solid, stress-free stay. We'll likely be back.

We had a wonderful long weekend at the Sofitel. The check-in was incredibly smooth, and we were greeted with a lovely welcome drink which set a warm tone. Our room was spacious and impeccably clean, with the classic French elegance you'd expect, but the bed was the real highlight - I slept like a log every night. The staff throughout the hotel were attentive without being intrusive; the concierge arranged a fantastic last-minute dinner reservation for us. Breakfast offered a great mix of pastries and hot dishes, and the coffee was top-notch. The only hiccup was a slightly slow elevator during a busy morning, but it was a minor issue. Location is perfect for exploring, yet the hotel feels like a peaceful sanctuary. We left feeling genuinely rested and would absolutely return.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have picked a better base. The room was spacious, spotless, and the bed was like sleeping on a cloud--I actually wanted to check out late just to enjoy it more. The staff made the difference though; from the doorman who remembered my name to the front desk helping me sort out a lost charger without any fuss, everyone seemed genuinely happy to help. The location is brilliant for sightseeing, but the real highlight was the breakfast spread--fresh pastries, made-to-order eggs, and the best coffee I had all trip. My only tiny gripe is the gym could use a few more free weights, but that's nitpicking. Would absolutely book again next time I'm in town.

My partner and I spent three nights here for our anniversary, and it was exactly the cozy, historic getaway we hoped for. The room was on the smaller side, but the wood beams, fireplace, and plush bedding made it feel like a warm hideaway rather than a cramped space. We loved that the hotel is right in the heart of the Magnificent Mile, yet our room was remarkably quiet--no street noise at all. The staff genuinely went out of their way, especially the concierge who booked us a last-minute river architecture tour and recommended an off-menu dish at a nearby bistro we still talk about. The complimentary breakfast was simple but well done, and the lobby's afternoon cookies were a lovely touch after a long walk. Sure, the building shows its age in a few nicks, but that's part of its charm. We left feeling rested, spoiled, and already planning a return. Highly recommend for couples who appreciate character over cookie-cutter hotels.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The lobby has a sleek, modern vibe that sets a nice tone. My room was spotless, with a super comfy bed and blackout curtains that actually worked--slept like a log. The location on East 39th is a huge win, super close to Grand Central and a quick stroll to Koreatown for late-night bites. Staff were friendly without being overbearing, and the check-in process was a breeze. Only tiny gripe: the bathroom could use a bit more counter space, but that's minor. The rooftop bar is a hidden gem with great city views. Would definitely book here again for the price point and convenience. Solid pick for a city trip.

My wife and I booked a last-minute weekend getaway and landed at Allegro, and honestly, it was a happy accident. The room was compact but spotless, and the bed was surprisingly comfy--I slept better here than at home. The real standout was the staff. From the front desk who let us check in early to the bartender who remembered our drink order on night two, everyone seemed genuinely happy to help. The rooftop pool is small but perfect for a lazy afternoon, and the included breakfast hit the spot every morning, especially the fresh-baked pastries. Location-wise, it's a quick walk to the tram and a few great local spots we found. The walls are a tad thin, and the shower pressure could be stronger, but for the price, this place overdelivers. We've already mentioned coming back.

We chose Hotel Amalfi for the view, but honestly, the staff made the stay. Every single person, from the front desk to the breakfast crew, greeted us by name after day one - a small touch that felt incredibly personal. The room itself was spotless, though the bathroom was a bit snug, a fair trade for the private balcony overlooking the water. Mornings were a highlight: strong espresso, flaky pastries, and a spread of local cheeses that fuelled our daily hikes. The only minor hiccup was the thin walls; we could hear our neighbours' late-night chatter. Still, the location is unbeatable - a five-minute stroll to the marina and tucked away from the main drag. I'd absolutely return for the hospitality alone.

We stayed for five nights at the Ambassador, and honestly, it exceeded what we expected from a city-center hotel. The moment we walked in, the doorman remembered our names from the second day on--that little personal touch meant a lot. Our room on the seventh floor was quiet, spotless, and had a brilliant view of the old town's rooftops, though the bathroom could've used a slightly stronger shower head. The breakfast spread was generous, with made-to-order omelets and pastries that stayed fresh. We had a minor issue with the air conditioning on the first evening, but the front desk sent a technician within ten minutes and followed up the next morning to make sure everything was fine. The pool area is small but pleasant, and the bar staff mix a solid negroni. If you want a comfortable, attentive stay without any fuss, this is it. We'd gladly return.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The room was spotless, with an incredibly comfortable bed and blackout curtains that made sleeping in feel glorious. The view of the river at sunset was a real highlight--I could have sat by the window all evening. Staff were professional without being stuffy; the concierge booked us a last-minute dinner spot that was fantastic. Breakfast had a good variety, though the coffee could have been stronger. The pool area was a bit crowded on Saturday afternoon, but that's my only minor gripe. Overall, a polished, relaxing stay that felt worth every penny. I'd happily return.

We had a fantastic stay at the Fairmont. The room was beautifully appointed with a super comfortable bed and a stunning view of the mountains. I was a bit worried about it being too formal, but the staff were so warm and welcoming, especially the concierge who helped us plan a last-minute hike.
