The breakfast buffet was a splurge but worth it for the sheer variety, from fresh pastries to made-to-order omelets. The pool area was a bit crowded in the afternoon, but we found it quiet in the early morning. Our only minor hiccup was a slow drain in the shower, but maintenance fixed it within twenty minutes of us calling. Overall, it was a classy and relaxing getaway that exceeded our expectations. We'd absolutely come back.

Stayed here for a long weekend celebrating my partner's birthday, and honestly, we were both blown away. The guitar-shaped tower is iconic, of course, but the vibe inside is what really sets it apart. We had a club-level room with a strip view, and the sunset over the palm trees was unreal - totally worth the upgrade. The staff at check-in were super friendly, even though the lobby was packed, and they surprised us with a small cake and a handwritten note for the occasion. We spent most of our time by the main pool - it gets busy, but the DJ kept the energy up and the cabana service was quick. Cocktails were strong and pricey, but you expect that. Dinner at the Mexican spot on property was surprisingly solid. Location can't be beaten for easy access to the strip, but the soundproofing meant we slept like babies. Would definitely book again for a special trip.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The room was spotless, the bed super comfortable, and the blackout curtains actually worked, which never happens. We had a minor issue with the AC on the first night, but housekeeping sorted it out within twenty minutes and even left a small fruit plate as an apology. The location is brilliant if you want to be near the waterfront, and the lobby bar makes a mean old fashioned. Breakfast buffet was pricier than I'd like, but the omelet station was worth it. Staff throughout were friendly without being overbearing. If you're after luxury, it's there, but it feels more like genuine hospitality than show. Would definitely book again.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have asked for a smoother visit. The suite was spotless and the kitchenette came in handy for late-night snacks, though the pull-out sofa was a touch firmer than I'd prefer. Breakfast had solid options--the make-your-own waffle station was a hit with the kids, and the scrambled eggs were actually fluffy, not rubbery. The indoor pool was warm, and the staff at the front desk remembered our room number every time we walked by, which felt personal. Location is convenient, about ten minutes from the interstate and a quick drive to a few decent restaurants. Only minor hiccup was the ice machine on our floor being out of order, but the guy at the desk offered to fill our cooler from the lobby without hesitation. I'd book here again for the value and the quiet, comfortable sleep.

Stayed for three nights during a conference and was genuinely impressed. The room was spotless, with a super comfortable bed and blackout curtains that actually worked--slept like a log. Staff at the front desk were efficient and friendly, even when the lobby was crowded. The in-house restaurant had a solid breakfast spread, and the omelet station was a nice touch. Location is a bit far from the main tourist drag, but the free shuttle to the downtown core made it easy. Gym is well-equipped, though the treadmills could use a tune-up. Pool area was quiet and clean. Only minor complaint: the Wi-Fi in the room dropped a couple of times during video calls. Otherwise, a dependable, comfortable stay that delivered on all the basics. Would book again for business trips.

Stayed for three nights to celebrate an anniversary, and honestly, they made it feel special without being fussy. The room was spotless with a ridiculously comfortable bed. I loved that the blackout curtains actually worked--slept past nine, which never happens. The pool area gets busy by late morning, so go early. Breakfast had a great mix of local and western options; the made-to-order omelet was a hit. Staff were attentive but not hovering. The location is perfect for walking to the old city, and the concierge gave us a fantastic, less-crowded route to the market. Only tiny gripe: the elevator wait during checkout was a bit long. Otherwise, a genuinely relaxing stay. Worth the splurge.

Stayed at Hotel James for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded every expectation I had. The location is perfect--steps from everything but tucked away enough to feel quiet. Check-in was a breeze; the front desk agent actually remembered my name and gave great dinner recommendations. The room itself was spotless, with a ridiculously comfortable bed and blackout curtains that let me sleep in past 9, which never happens. I loved the little touches: the complimentary coffee in the lobby each morning was strong and delicious, and the gym was way better equipped than most hotels I've visited. The only minor hiccup was the shower pressure fluctuating one evening, but it didn't ruin anything. The bar downstairs has a fantastic cocktail list, and the staff there were friendly without being pushy. For the price, this place is a steal. I've already booked my next stay for next month. Can't recommend it enough.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, the location is unbeatable. You're right in the middle of everything, steps from the river walk, and the views from the upper floors are stunning at sunset. The room itself was a bit on the compact side, but the bed was incredibly comfortable and the blackout curtains worked wonders. What really impressed me was the staff--every single person, from the doorman to the front desk, was genuinely friendly and helpful without being overbearing. The rooftop bar is a must-visit, even if you're not a guest, though the cocktails are pricey. My only minor gripe was the hallway noise in the mornings, but it wasn't a dealbreaker. I'd absolutely book again for the charm and convenience.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have picked a better spot. The location is unbeatable--steps from the riverfront and a short stroll to all the good restaurants, but the street itself stays quiet at night, which I appreciated. Check-in was smooth, and they even let us into our room early since we'd arrived before the standard time. The room itself was stylish without feeling stuffy, and the bed was genuinely comfortable; I slept like a log both nights. Bathroom had great water pressure and those little toiletries that actually smell nice. The bar downstairs is worth a visit even if you're not a guest--the bartender mixed a killer Old Fashioned. Only tiny gripe: the hallway ice machine was out on our floor, but the front desk sent someone up with a bucket within minutes. Would gladly book again.

We had a wonderful three-night stay at the Omni. The location was perfect for exploring the city, but honestly, we could have just stayed in the hotel the whole time. The pool area was a real highlight--clean, well-heated, and the towels were always stocked. Our room was spotless and the bed was incredibly comfortable; I slept better than I do at home. The staff were all so welcoming, from the valet to the front desk. We had one small issue with the TV remote and someone was up to fix it within minutes. Breakfast on the terrace was a lovely way to start the day. We're already looking at dates to come back next year.

We stayed at Hotel Palmer for four nights and honestly couldn't have been happier with the choice. The location is perfect--a quiet street but still a five-minute walk to the main square, which meant we got peaceful mornings without being isolated. Our room overlooked a small courtyard, and the soundproofing was excellent; we never heard a peep from the neighbors. The bed was firm but supportive, and the blackout curtains worked wonders after late nights. Breakfast was a highlight: fresh pastries, local cheeses, and made-to-order eggs that weren't swimming in grease. The staff remembered our preferences by the second day, which felt genuinely thoughtful rather than scripted. Only minor hiccup was the shower pressure being a bit weak, but the water stayed hot. We'd absolutely return and would recommend it to anyone wanting a comfortable, unpretentious base.

Checked in a bit later than planned, around 10 PM, and the front desk had everything ready--even upgraded us to a high floor with a nice view of the river, which was a lovely surprise. The room was spotless, bed super comfy, and the blackout curtains actually worked. Breakfast buffet had a good mix of hot and cold options; the omelet station was a plus, though the coffee could've been stronger. I used the gym in the morning--it's compact but had everything I needed. Location is solid for exploring, with the metro a short walk. Only minor gripe: the hallway ice machine was noisy at night, but it didn't ruin anything. Staff were consistently friendly, from valet to housekeeping. I'd gladly stay here again for the value and reliability.

We booked the Sofitel for a anniversary weekend and honestly couldn't have picked better. The room was spacious, with a heavenly bed and a view of the city lights that made us feel like we were in a movie. The staff were professional but warm, especially the concierge who arranged a last-minute dinner reservation for us at a lovely bistro. The pool area was a serene escape from the busy streets, and we spent a lazy afternoon there. Breakfast had everything we could crave, from fresh pastries to made-to-order omelets. While the lobby was a bit busy at check-in, the efficient process made up for it. We left feeling completely relaxed and already planning our return. A truly elegant stay with that special touch you don't find everywhere.

The location is unbeatable for sightseeing, right by the river and a short stroll to the Old Town. We booked a standard room and were pleasantly surprised by the space, plus the soundproofing was perfect--slept like a baby despite the bustling city outside. The breakfast spread deserves a special mention: fresh pastries, made-to-order eggs, and a great selection of local cheeses. Staff were professional and friendly, quickly sorting out an extra pillow request and recommending a fantastic restaurant for dinner. My only minor gripe was the slightly slow Wi-Fi in the evenings, but it didn't ruin anything. The gym is small but well-equipped, and the pool area is a nice bonus after a long day of walking. For the price and quality, I would definitely stay here again on my next trip.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, I'm still thinking about the bed. That mattress was pure cloud--slept like a log all three nights, which never happens in hotels. Location is unbeatable: two blocks from the river, easy walk to all the good coffee spots, and quiet enough at night. The front desk guy, Marcus, remembered our names and had great tips for a hidden speakeasy we'd have never found. Room was compact but smartly laid out, with a rainfall shower that had serious pressure. Breakfast was simple--pastries, fruit, decent espresso--but the fresh orange juice was a lovely touch. Only tiny gripe: the hallway ice machine was out of order one afternoon. Minor. Would absolutely book again for the location and that heavenly bed.

We booked Affinia expecting a polished stay, but it felt more like a faded chain trying too hard. Breakfast was a cramped buffet of lukewarm scrambled eggs and stale pastries, and the coffee tasted burnt. The wifi dropped constantly, making it impossible to stream anything or even load a basic map without frustration. Our room faced an interior airshaft, so the 'view' was just a brick wall and a humming vent. Noise was the worst part--thin walls meant every hallway conversation and door slam echoed through the night, and we got little sleep. The bed was decent, but that's about the only compliment. Staff were polite but couldn't resolve the internet or offer a quieter floor. For the price they charge, this was a letdown. I'd look elsewhere unless you're desperate and don't mind feeling like you're in a budget hostel with nicer curtains.

I booked the Hotel Allegro hoping for a charming boutique stay, but the reality was a letdown from the moment I checked in. The front desk agent barely acknowledged me, handing over the key card with a curt nod and zero information about the property. My room, while visually okay at first glance, had a suspicious stain on the carpet near the window and a layer of dust on the headboard. The bathroom was the worst part: the shower pressure was a pathetic trickle, and the grout between the tiles was black with mold. I couldn't even enjoy the much-talked-about view--all I saw was a brick wall and a noisy ventilation unit grumbling outside. The location is convenient, but the apathetic staff and tired, dirty rooms made it feel like a glorified hostel. I would not return.

I had high hopes for Hotel Amalfi, but honestly, the experience left a sour taste. The room itself was passable at first glance, but the carpet had a sticky patch near the mini-fridge, and there was a suspicious, damp smell that lingered the entire time. Our one-night stay ended up feeling interminable, mostly because the air conditioning unit rattled like a coffee grinder all night, making sleep nearly impossible.

The staff were polite enough at check-in, but whenever we called down for extra towels or a wake-up call, we were met with a dismissive tone and long holds. The bathroom was the worst offender: the showerhead sprayed in a weak, erratic pattern, and the grouting had gone a worrying shade of black. Plus, the exhaust fan didn't work, leaving the room steamy and muggy. For the price, I expected far more, and I cannot recommend this place.

I booked the Ambassador expecting a bit of a splurge, but honestly, I left feeling like I'd thrown money away. The room rate was steep, and for that price, I expected something more than a worn carpet and furniture that looked like it hadn't been updated since the early 2000s. The mustard-yellow armchair had a suspicious stain, and the curtains smelled faintly of dust. Our window faced a brick wall, so 'view' was a generous term--we had to keep the blinds shut for any privacy, which made the room feel like a cave. The staff were polite but overwhelmed, and the breakfast buffet was a sad spread of stale pastries. I was only there for one night, yet that was more than enough. Two nights would have felt like a punishment. Not worth the premium, not by a long shot.

I had high hopes for the Conrad, but honestly, the experience left me frustrated. The bathroom was the first letdown--a single, shallow sink that splashed water everywhere and a showerhead with only two settings, one of which dribbled. The room itself wasn't truly dirty, but there were dust bunnies under the desk and a suspicious stain on the armchair I didn't want to examine closely. Staff were polite at check-in but completely dismissive when I asked for extra towels, telling me to call housekeeping myself; when I did, no one ever answered. Despite the 'city view' promise, I heard constant hallway chatter, slamming doors, and what sounded like furniture being dragged upstairs until nearly 2 AM. For these rates, I expected polish and attention--instead I got a mediocre stay that felt more like a mid-tier business hotel. I won't be returning.

I'd been looking forward to a special weekend at the Fairmont, but the reality fell far short of the pictures and the price tag. Our room on the eighth floor faced the parking garage and a slice of rooftops; we had to lean out the window to see any skyline, and even then, it was mostly cranes. The hallway noise was relentless--doors slamming and guests talking loudly until past midnight, and thin walls meant we heard every flush from next door. At over four hundred a night, it felt like a robbery for what was essentially a mediocre business hotel. The front desk staff were polite but disinterested, and when I asked about a quieter room, they shrugged and said the hotel was full. Housekeeping skipped our turn-down entirely, and the one call I made to request extra towels rang for ages before someone picked up. I truly wanted to love it, but I left feeling cheated and exhausted.

I've stayed at Hard Rock properties before and usually expect a certain level of polish, but this visit missed the mark by a mile. The bathroom looked decent at first, but the shower drain was slow, and the cheap pump bottles of soap were nearly empty. Our 'city view' turned out to be a brick wall and a vent that hummed all night. Staff were polite at check-in but vanished when we called for extra towels--took three tries and over an hour. Sleep was rough: the mattress sagged in the middle, and the hallway noise from a rowdy group carried straight through the thin door. For the price, this felt more like a mid-tier chain than a rock-and-roll flagship. I wanted to love it, but left tired and frustrated. Won't be back.

The view from my 14th-floor room was the only thing that didn't disappoint--a hazy slice of the skyline that felt wasted on a window I barely had time to enjoy. My three-night business stay stretched into an eternity of restless evenings, the bed too firm and the hallway noise relentless until past midnight. I would have traded half that time for functioning internet; the complimentary Wi-Fi dropped every twenty minutes, forcing me to re-login repeatedly while trying to join a video call. The staff, though polite at check-in, vanished when I asked for a late checkout--and the front desk agent who finally appeared seemed annoyed, barely glancing up from her screen. The hallways smelled faintly of stale coffee, and the air conditioning rattled like a loose shutter. For the price, I expected far more than a good view and a lukewarm hello.

We booked Homewood expecting a decent night's sleep before an early flight, but it was a real letdown. The hallway noise was constant well past midnight--doors slamming, people talking at full volume--and the walls were paper-thin. I could hear the TV from the room next door as if it were on my nightstand. The wifi was practically useless; it kept dropping and was too slow to even load a basic webpage, which I needed for work. Honestly, for what they charged, I felt ripped off. The room itself was shabby, with a stained carpet and a worn-out mattress that sagged in the middle. I tossed and turned all night and woke up more exhausted than when I arrived. Save your money and stay elsewhere.

I booked the Hyatt expecting the usual level of polish, but left genuinely frustrated. Our room faced a construction site, so the 'city view' was mostly a crane and a lot of dust. The noise was relentless--jackhammering started before 7 AM, and the thin windows did nothing to muffle it. I barely slept; by the second night, I was counting the hours until checkout, and honestly, the three nights felt like a week. The hallways weren't much better, with slamming doors echoing until midnight. I'll give credit to the front desk clerk who moved us to a higher floor, but it still didn't help. The bed itself was decent, but that's about all. For the price, I expected far more. I won't be back.

I booked the InterContinental expecting a touch of grandeur, but the reality felt like a faded postcard. The lobby's marble gleams, sure, but the hallway carpets are worn, and the room's furniture looks straight out of the late '90s, with scuffed edges and a tired floral armchair. The bed was comfortable enough, but the cleanliness was spotty--I found a stale receipt under the desk and dust bunnies lurking by the baseboards. Our one-night stop felt both rushed and interminable; the paper-thin walls let me hear every door slam and hallway conversation, so I got little rest. The bathroom was the low point: a cracked tile, a showerhead with uneven pressure, and a faint musty smell that no amount of ventilation could fix. For this price, I expected polish, not patina. I won't return.

I booked the James for a special weekend, and honestly, it fell flat. The location is decent--you can walk to the river and a few good spots--but that's the only saving grace. Our bathroom was the real letdown: a cracked tile in the shower, lukewarm water pressure that sputtered, and a sink that drained so slowly I had to brush my teeth in the tub. The room itself looked tidy at first, but the carpet had visible stains near the window, and I found a stray hair on the duvet. Staff were polite enough, yet when I mentioned the bathroom issue at the front desk, the response was a shrug and a promise to 'note it' that never materialized. For the price, I expected more polish. It wasn't a disaster--just a list of small disappointments that added up to a stay I won't be repeating.

I was really looking forward to a weekend getaway, but the Knickerbocker left me feeling more tired than when I arrived. The bed was rock hard, and the constant hum from the street traffic meant I was up half the night. Breakfast was a sad affair of lukewarm, rubbery eggs and stale pastries, served by a staff that seemed completely indifferent. The bathroom had a perpetually clogged drain that left the floor wet, and the water pressure in the shower was pathetically weak. We paid extra for a city view, but our window looked directly over a noisy construction site and a grim airshaft, offering just a sliver of the skyline. Overall, it was a disappointing stay that felt far overpriced for the quality. I wouldn't recommend it.

I'm not sure if the walls are paper-thin or if my neighbors were just having a full-blown party, but I heard every thump and laugh until nearly 2 a.m. For nearly $300 a night, I expected better soundproofing. The room itself was clean and stylish, but that didn't make up for the constant noise, nor the lukewarm breakfast where the scrambled eggs were dry and the coffee tasted burnt. The location is convenient, but I felt the whole experience was wildly overpriced, almost like paying for a luxury brand without the substance. My two nights felt like an eternity, and by the second morning I was counting the hours until checkout. If you crave peace and value, look elsewhere.

The Omni left me feeling genuinely underwhelmed. The bathroom was cramped, with a showerhead that dribbled water sideways and a towel rack that fell off the wall when I reached for a fresh one. My 'city view' turned out to be a direct line into an office building's HVAC units, so I kept the curtains drawn the entire time. The wifi was a sore spot--connection dropped constantly, making it impossible to stream anything or even hold a simple video call for work. Oddly, my two-night stay felt both too short and too long: too short to offset the travel hassle, but too long after the third cold shower and the fourth hour of internet frustration. The bed was comfortable, I'll grant that, but this was not the relaxing retreat I'd booked. I left more stressed than when I arrived, and I won't be returning.

The Palmer's location on State Street is genuinely hard to beat for sightseeing, which is the only reason I'm giving it two stars instead of one. Unfortunately, that's where the positives end. Our room, advertised as recently renovated, looked tired and worn, with a suspicious stain on the carpet near the mini-fridge and a layer of dust on the headboard. The bathroom was the real letdown--the shower pressure was pitiful, the grout was discolored, and the provided toiletries smelled like cheap generic soap. Housekeeping did the bare minimum, leaving wet towels on the floor and not replacing the coffee. At $280 a night, this felt like a $90 motel experience dressed up in a fancy lobby. The location saved the trip, but the value simply wasn't there.

Checked in at 3 PM, but the room wasn't ready until nearly 5, and no one offered so much as a complimentary drink while we waited in the crowded lobby. The wifi was practically useless in our room--kept dropping every few minutes, making any work impossible. Staff were polite but visibly overwhelmed, and my request for extra towels took three calls and an hour. For the premium rate we paid, the carpet looked stained and the bathroom had a lingering musty smell. We booked three nights, but by the second morning, we were already counting the hours to checkout. The location is convenient, sure, but this felt like a $120 motel experience dressed up with a fancy lobby. I'd rather have skipped the last night entirely than paid what they charged. Genuinely disappointing for a brand I once trusted.

I booked the Sofitel expecting Parisian elegance, but left feeling thoroughly underwhelmed. The hallway carpet looked tired, and our room's decor felt stuck in the early 2000s--stiff beige fabrics, a bulky armoire, and lighting so dim it was hard to read. Worse, the air conditioner rattled all night, and I barely slept; the thin walls let every hallway conversation seep through. Housekeeping was inconsistent: the bathroom floor had a stray hair on arrival, and the glass shower door was smeared with fingerprints. I asked for a quiet floor at check-in, yet we faced a busy street where sirens blared until 3 a.m. The bed itself was comfortable enough, but that's the only positive. For this price point, I expect freshness, soundproofing, and meticulous cleaning--none of which were delivered. I won't be returning.

I booked the Swissotel expecting the dependable quality that comes with the brand name, but my stay left me genuinely underwhelmed. Our room faced the internal courtyard, and while that meant it was mercifully quiet, the view was essentially a grey wall and the top of the mechanical plant room. The bathroom felt like an afterthought from the early nineties, with a clunky, cracked tiled surround and a shower head that sprayed in every direction except on me. The carpet in the hallway had visible stains, and the room itself, despite the recent refurbishment claims, still had dated, beige furniture that creaked ominously. Honestly, for the nightly rate, I expected far more polish. You're paying for the location and the name, but the experience itself felt tired. I would think twice before booking here again, especially since there are fresher, better-value options a few blocks away. It wasn't a disaster, but it was a disappointment.

The Talbotts' worn glamour is charming from the lobby, but that charm evaporates by the second night. Our 'deluxe' room had a frayed carpet and a window facing a brick wall, so I slept poorly, disturbed by hallway noise and an AC unit that rattled like a loose muffler. The staff were polite but overwhelmed; housekeeping ignored our door sign twice, and front desk claimed they couldn't fix the thermostat until the next day. At $340 a night, this felt like a $190 experience. We checked out after only one of our two planned nights--not because the stay was too short, but because the mattress sagged and the bathroom smelled faintly of mildew. The location and vintage bar are lovely, but you're paying for history, not comfort. I'd pass on a return.

The Affinia left me genuinely puzzled. The location was undeniably its only saving grace--steps from the El and a short cab ride to the Loop made sightseeing easy. Inside, though, the decor felt frozen in the mid-2000s, with tired floral patterns on the bedding and a hallway carpet that had seen better decades. My bathroom was the low point: the showerhead had only two settings (dribble or scalding blast), and the grout looked like it hadn't seen a scrub brush in months. The staff were polite but perpetually overstretched; the front desk gave clipped answers to my questions about dining, and housekeeping knocked at 8:30 AM despite my 'Do Not Disturb' sign. For what they charge, I expected polish, not this faded, disengaged experience. I won't be back.

Breakfast was the first letdown of the day--cold scrambled eggs that looked like they'd been sitting out since dawn, plus coffee that tasted burnt and watery. I slept terribly, partly because the mattress sagged in the middle and partly because I could hear every footstep in the hallway, as if the walls were made of paper. The staff seemed perpetually annoyed; asking for extra towels earned me a sigh and a slow, grudging walk to the supply closet. The lobby decor hasn't been touched since the mid-2000s--faded floral carpet, wobbly armchairs, and a strange, cloying air freshener. By the second night, I just wanted to leave. For the price, you'd expect at least a decent night's rest and a smile from the front desk. This place delivered neither.

I'd heard the Amalfi's location was unbeatable, and that much is true--you're steps from the old town. But that's where the positives end. The 'sea view' we paid extra for was mostly a rooftop and a sliver of water, and the window hadn't been cleaned in months. Check-in took forever, and the front desk clerk seemed annoyed by every question. The room itself felt trapped in 1985, with mustard-toned carpet, a tiny tube TV, and a showerhead that dribbled. Housekeeping never replaced the coffee pods, and the hair dryer died on day two. When I asked for a late checkout, I got a flat 'no' without apology. Honestly, the building's location is the only thing working in its favor. For the price, you could do much better a few blocks over. I left feeling tired, dusty, and thoroughly unimpressed.

I really wanted to like the Hotel Ambassador, but our anniversary weekend fell flat. The lobby's plastic plants and stained carpet set the tone; our room followed suit with floral drapes from another decade and a radiator that clanked all night. We paid extra for a 'city view,' which was mostly a brick wall and a sliver of rooftop. The staff were polite but indifferent--at check-in we were handed keys without a smile or a single recommendation, and housekeeping never replaced our empty coffee pods. The bathroom was the worst part: a cracked tub with poor water pressure, a loose faucet, and a hairdryer that died mid-use. The bed was comfortable, I'll give them that, but the peeling wallpaper and gum under the desk made us eager to leave. For these prices, you can do much better.

I was really looking forward to a luxurious weekend at the Conrad, but it fell short in every meaningful way. The noise was the first problem--our room faced the street, and sirens and traffic kept me up until 2 a.m. despite the advertised soundproofing. The bathroom looked nice at first, but the shower pressure was dismal, and the glass door leaked water all over the floor. Breakfast was a crowded, chaotic buffet with lukewarm eggs and stale pastries; the omelet station had a 20-minute wait. Worst of all, the Wi-Fi kept dropping every ten minutes, and the front desk suggested I 'move closer to the router.' For nearly $400 a night, I expected calm, comfort, and functioning basics. Instead, I left exhausted and annoyed. I won't be returning.

I booked the Fairmont expecting a landmark stay, but left feeling I'd overpaid for a faded name. The bed was decent, but the air conditioning cycled loudly all night, and I woke up more tired than when I arrived. At nearly $400 a night, that alone stung. The lobby has grand bones, yet the hallways and our room feel stuck in the early 2000s--scuffed baseboards, worn carpet, and furniture that looks like it survived a decade of conferences. Breakfast was the low point: a lukewarm buffet with watery scrambled eggs and stale pastries, all for $32 a head. Service was polite but stretched thin, especially at check-in. Honestly, the location is prime, but so is the competition. For this price, I expected polish, not a lesson in managing disappointment. I won't be back.

I booked the Hard Rock hoping for a fun, rock-and-roll vibe, but what I got was a tired, overpriced room that felt like a generic budget hotel with a guitar decal slapped on the wall. The bathroom was the worst part: the shower head dripped constantly, the grout was stained dark in the corners, and the tiny mirror was fogged up for a full hour after any hot water ran. Honestly, at over $300 a night, this was a total rip-off. The room itself had crumbs on the carpet near the mini-fridge and a suspicious sticky patch by the desk that housekeeping clearly missed. As for noise, forget sleeping in--the hallway thumped with bass from a party until 3 AM, and the ice machine on our floor rattled like a broken snare drum all night. The only thing 'hard' about this stay was the bed, which felt like a concrete slab. Save your money and pick somewhere else.

Checked in after a long flight and was met by a front desk agent who barely looked up, muttering through the process as if I were interrupting something. The room itself felt tired--carpet stained near the window, a layer of dust on the nightstand, and the bathroom grout looked like it hadn't seen a scrub brush in weeks. The Wi-Fi dropped three times during a single video call, forcing me to restart the whole session. Location is decent if you want to be near the convention center, but it's a hike to any decent restaurant or bar. Honestly, for the price, I expected far more polish. I've stayed at better-run Hiltons in smaller cities. I won't be returning to this one.

You can't beat the location for exploring downtown, which was the only saving grace. Unfortunately, the stay felt about two nights too long once the issues piled up. Breakfast was a chaotic zoo--the scrambled eggs were watery, the coffee urn ran dry twice, and the 'hot' oatmeal was lukewarm by the time I found a table. Sleep was nearly impossible: the AC unit clanked all night, and the walls were so thin I heard every toilet flush from the adjacent room. The bed sagged in the middle, and the pillows were flat as pancakes. I checked out a day early, honestly. For the price, I expected basic comfort. Instead, I left exhausted and disappointed. A convenient spot wasted on a rundown property. I won't be back.

Checked in around 4pm and the front desk agent barely looked up from her screen, handing over the key card without a single question about our stay. The room itself was a letdown--dust bunnies in the corners, a sticky spot on the nightstand, and the bathroom mirror had smudges that looked like they hadn't been wiped in days. Breakfast the next morning was borderline sad: lukewarm scrambled eggs, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt, all served in a dining area that felt cramped and grimy. The decor throughout felt trapped in the early 2000s--beige carpets, dated floral patterns, and worn furniture that desperately needed replacing. Even the hallway smelled faintly of old carpet cleaner. For the price we paid, I expected far more polish and attention. Disappointing overall, and I'm honestly not sure I'd return even if the location is convenient.

I booked the Intercontinental expecting the grandeur its name implies, but what I found was a faded echo of a bygone era. The lobby is impressive, sure, but my room felt stuck in the 90s, with worn carpet and furniture that looked tired rather than classic. The staff were courteous but overwhelmed; a simple request for extra towels took three calls and nearly an hour. While the location is undeniably convenient, just steps from the Magnificent Mile, that's its only saving grace. My window faced a brick wall and an air conditioning unit, offering a view that was frankly depressing. For the premium price, this felt like a letdown. I honestly expected far more polish for a property of this stature. I left feeling I'd overpaid for a name, not an experience, and I would think twice before returning.

We booked the James expecting a sleek, quiet retreat, but our stay was a letdown from start to finish. The room faced an interior airshaft, so the 'city view' was basically a brick wall and a glimpse of the neighboring rooftop AC units. Worse, the hallways were surprisingly noisy--we heard shouting and slamming doors until past 2 AM, and the thin window did nothing to block the mechanical hum. Housekeeping clearly skipped the details: there was a sticky patch near the mini-fridge, dust on the lampshades, and a coffee ring on the desk. I slept poorly, tossing all night on a mattress that sagged in the middle, and the pillows were limp as pancakes. By morning, I was exhausted and just wanted out. For the price, this felt more like a budget chain than a boutique stay. I won't be returning.

I booked the Knickerbocker expecting old-world charm, but the reality felt more like neglect. Our room faced the interior airshaft, so the 'city view' was a brick wall and a humming vent, which also meant we heard every conversation from neighboring rooms and the clatter of housekeeping carts from 7 AM. At nearly $400 a night, it was a real gut punch. The carpet was stained, the furniture had that dusty, faded look from the 90s, and the single elevator was perpetually packed. The lobby is grand, sure, but the rooms don't match the facade. The location on the Mag Mile is the only saving grace, but it doesn't excuse the noise, the dated decor, or the feeling that the staff couldn't care less. I'd skip it unless you're desperate for the address.

The location was genuinely convenient, steps from the metro and a host of decent eateries, which made getting around painless. That's where the positives end. My room felt tired, but the bathroom was the real low point: the showerhead spat unevenly, the grout was dark and grimy, and the ventilation fan rattled all night. Breakfast was a sad buffet of lukewarm scrambled eggs, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt. To top it off, the wifi dropped constantly, forcing me to hotspot my phone for work. I'm not sure what's changed, but this didn't live up to the brand's reputation. A serviceable mattress and friendly front desk staff couldn't rescue a stay that left me counting down to checkout. I'd only return if nowhere else was available.

I booked the Omni expecting the polished, upscale vibe the photos promised, but the reality was a frayed version of that. The front desk staff were painfully indifferent, barely looking up from their screens to hand over the key card, and every request for extra towels or a late checkout was met with a curt 'we'll see.' The wifi was a joke--it dropped constantly in the room, forcing me to camp in the lobby just to send a simple email, which hardly feels acceptable at these rates. Honestly, the price tag felt absurd for what I got. The bathroom was the worst part: a cracked tile near the tub, a showerhead that sprayed sideways, and a lingering musty odor no amount of fan noise could fix. I've had better stays at mid-range chains for half the cost. This was a disappointing, overpriced miss.

I booked the Hotel Palmer based on photos that promised charm, but the reality was a letdown from the start. The bed was rock hard, and the thin pillows left me tossing until 3 AM; I woke up with a stiff neck and a headache. The Wi-Fi was essentially a rumor--it dropped every few minutes, making it impossible to even load a simple email. While the hallway was quiet, the walls were paper-thin, and I heard every flush and conversation from the neighboring room until midnight. The bathroom was the worst offender: the showerhead sputtered with uneven pressure, and the sink had a stubborn clog that left water standing for hours. I'm not one to complain, but for the price, this stay felt like a complete waste of money. I won't be back.

I booked the Sheraton expecting the dependable comfort of a big-name chain, but the experience left a sour taste. The moment I walked into the lobby, the dated floral carpets and worn armchairs screamed 1990s, and the hallways had a faint musty smell. My room was a mixed bag: the bathroom sparkled, but the carpet by the bed had a suspicious dark stain I avoided stepping on, and the curtains were frayed at the edges. I slept terribly--the mattress sagged in the middle, and the air conditioner rattled loudly every few minutes, keeping me half-awake all night. Breakfast was the final letdown: lukewarm scrambled eggs that tasted powdered, stale croissants, and coffee that was weak and bitter. For nearly $250 a night, I'd expect modern fixtures, a truly clean floor, and at least decent morning fuel. Sadly, this felt more like a budget motel with a fancy sign. I won't be returning.

My stay at the Sofitel was a masterclass in under-delivery. The promise of Parisian elegance faded the moment I stepped off the elevator onto my floor, where the hallway hummed with a persistent, mechanical drone--a sound that followed me into my room, where the air conditioning unit clattered all night. Sleep was fitful; I woke up more exhausted than when I arrived. The two nights stretched on interminably. Staff were polite but maddeningly disengaged; my request for a later checkout was met with a shrug and a curt 'possible, but not guaranteed.' The one saving grace, the panoramic view of the city, was perpetually obscured by a film of grime on the window I couldn't reach. It felt like being trapped in a beautiful, broken spaceship. I finally checked out feeling shortchanged, as if the visit had been a dull, lengthy obligation rather than a brief escape.

We booked the Swissotel based on its reputation, but the whole experience felt tired. The hallway carpet was worn, and our room's decor looked like it hadn't been updated since the early 2000s - beige, scuffed, and with a lampshade that was crooked. I slept poorly, partly because the mattress sagged in the middle and partly because the air conditioning hummed loudly every ten minutes. On the bright side, the windows were well-insulated, so street noise wasn't the issue. What really got me was how long the stay felt; we had booked for three nights but checked out after two because there was simply nothing enjoyable to linger over. The staff was polite but overstretched, and the breakfast buffet ran out of everything by 9 a.m. I can't call it a disaster, just a persistent, drab disappointment that made me wish we'd picked another property.

I was really looking forward to our weekend at the Talbott, but the experience left me flat. The front desk staff seemed almost annoyed by our presence, barely looking up from their screens during check-in. The decor is stuck in the early 90s, with tired floral patterns and worn carpet in the hallways that smells faintly of dust. Our room faced the back alley, so the 'city view' was really just a brick wall and a dumpster. The bed was saggy, and the constant humming from the HVAC unit made it impossible to fall asleep until late. I woke up more tired than when I arrived. For this price, I genuinely expect better service and a decent night's rest. I would not return, which is a shame because the location is convenient.

I booked two nights at Affinia as a weekend escape, and honestly, I'm relieved it wasn't a week. The room's window faced an interior air shaft, offering a grim view of concrete and a humming exhaust fan, which I stared at more than I'd like because the Wi-Fi kept dropping every few minutes on my laptop. Traffic noise from the street seeped through the glass all night, so rest was elusive--I heard every siren and motorcycle until 3 a.m. The stay felt both cramped and overlong, as the tiny bathroom and worn carpet made me eager to leave by checkout. Front desk staff were polite but couldn't fix the connectivity or offer a quieter room. For the price, this was a letdown; I'd look elsewhere next time.

I really wanted to like the Hotel Allegro, but it felt like a missed opportunity at every turn. The location is fine, but walking into the room felt like stepping back into 1992, with tired floral curtains and worn, scuffed furniture that absolutely did not match the photos online. Cleanliness was a major letdown; I found a hair on the pillowcase and the bathroom grout was stained and grimy. The breakfast was chaotic and cheap--powdered eggs, stale pastries, and lukewarm coffee that ran out quickly. Honestly, the place felt overpriced for what you get, especially when there are better options nearby. The bed was comfortable enough, but that's the only positive. The hallways had a strange, musty odor, too. For the money I spent, I expected a charming, updated boutique experience, but instead I left feeling relieved to check out. I can't recommend it unless you're purely after a bed for one night.

My stay at Hotel Amalfi was, frankly, a letdown from the moment I walked in. The 'boutique charm' advertised online translates to dark, cramped hallways and a lobby that smelled like stale cooking oil. My room faced the main road, and the noise was relentless--scooters revving and car horns blaring through the flimsy windows until past midnight. I barely slept. What little rest I got was on a mattress that sagged in the middle, and the pillow was as flat as a pancake. Breakfast the next morning was the final straw: lukewarm scrambled eggs, rubbery croissants, and coffee that tasted burnt. I found myself counting the hours until checkout, yet the check-in process was so slow I felt my vacation slipping away before it began. Given the price, I expected far more. Certainly not a stay I'd recommend.

I booked the Ambassador expecting a quiet, central base, but between the rattling elevator shaft and the street-level bar's bass thumping until 2 AM, I barely got three hours of sleep. The room itself was clean enough, but the walls were paper-thin--I could hear the neighbor's TV news and every flush. The staff seemed overwhelmed and disinterested; my request for a fan to mask the noise was met with a shrug and a promise that never materialized. Location-wise, you can't beat the walk to the main square, but that's about all it has going for it. Check-in took twenty minutes, and the front desk didn't even acknowledge my loyalty status. I left more exhausted than I arrived, paying a premium for a night that felt like a dormitory. Unless you're a heavy sleeper or bring earplugs, I'd look elsewhere. Disappointing all around.

I booked the Conrad expecting a premium experience, but the reality fell far short of the price tag. The location is genuinely excellent, right in the heart of things, which is the only reason I'd rate it two stars instead of one. However, the value for money is poor; our 'deluxe' room felt tired, with dated furniture and a musty smell despite the inflated rate. The noise was a constant issue all night long--thin walls meant I could hear the neighboring guest's television and every hallway conversation, and the street traffic below kept my windows vibrating. Staff interactions felt transactional and cold. At check-in, I was handed a key without a smile or any acknowledgment of our anniversary, and when I asked for a quiet room or a later checkout, I was brushed off without empathy. It's a shame, because the property has potential, but this wasn't worth the splurge.

I booked the Fairmont expecting a touch of elegance, but what I got was a masterclass in indifference. Breakfast was a chaotic, overpriced buffet where the scrambled eggs were cold and the coffee tasted burnt; getting a server's attention felt like a minor miracle. The staff, when they weren't avoiding eye contact, were curt to the point of rudeness, especially at the front desk during check-in. The location is admittedly convenient for sightseeing, but that's the only positive. My bathroom had peeling caulk around the tub and a hair dryer that barely worked, plus the water pressure in the shower was laughably weak. For the nightly rate, I expected polished service and clean details. Instead, I left with a bitter aftertaste and a lighter wallet. I won't be returning.

Stayed here over a long weekend and left feeling thoroughly underwhelmed, especially for the nightly rate. The Wi-Fi was a joke--constantly dropping in the room, so I ended up tethering my laptop to my phone just to get work done. That's not acceptable at these prices. Breakfast was a cramped, chaotic buffet where the scrambled eggs were rubbery and the coffee tasted burnt; we waited fifteen minutes just for a table. Location is decent, right near the strip and easy walking to attractions, but everything else drags it down. The room itself felt worn, with stained carpet and a bathroom that smelled musty. I wasn't expecting luxury, but I was expecting basic competence. For what we paid, this was a rip-off. I won't be back.

Breakfast was a cringe-worthy affair: lukewarm scrambled eggs that tasted of nothing, stale pastries, and coffee that was closer to dishwater. The wifi flickered in and out so unpredictably that I gave up trying to stream anything and just stared at my phone's 'no connection' icon. Oddly, our three-night stay felt both interminable and rushed -- endless hours of nothing to do in the room, yet checkout arrived before we'd ever relaxed. The noise was the real killer: walls thin enough to hear the neighbor's TV and a hallway that echoed with slammed doors until 2 a.m. For Hilton's reputation, this was a profound letdown. I left more exhausted than when I arrived, and I won't be back.

The bed was advertised as plush, but it felt like a lumpy sack of potatoes, and I woke up every hour with a stiff back. The whole place has a sad, early-2000s vibe, with worn carpet in the hallways and furniture that looks like it survived a frat party. At nearly two hundred a night, I expected better; this felt more like a budget motel with a fancy lobby. Our window faced the parking garage and a dumpster, so we kept the curtains shut the entire time. The noise from the HVAC unit rattled all night, too. Honestly, the only positive was the front desk clerk, who was friendly but couldn't fix the fundamental issues. I left more exhausted than when I arrived, and I definitely won't be back. Save your money.

Checked in after midnight to find the hallway reeked of stale cigarette smoke, and the smell crept right under the door into our room. The bathroom was the worst part--the showerhead sprayed sideways, the caulk around the tub was peeling and gray, and the hairdryer sounded like a dying lawnmower. Housekeeping clearly missed this one: there was a sticky patch near the minibar and what looked like crumbs under the desk. Location is decent if you want the Loop, but you're paying for that address alone. I could hear every door slam and the elevator ding until 2 a.m., plus the HVAC rattled on and off all night. Bed was firm, sheets were clean, but that's the only positive. For Hyatt's name, this was a letdown--dirty, dated, and far from restful. I won't be back.

I'd heard the Intercontinental name carries weight, so I expected more than what I got. The room faced the inner courtyard, which was eerily quiet at night--until 6 a.m., when housekeeping carts rumbled down the corridor like a freight train. I slept in fits, never reaching that deep rest you hope for when traveling. The WiFi was a joke: patched into the lobby network, it dropped every time I turned my phone, and the in-room 'high-speed' option required a login that expired hourly. For the price, I felt cheated. The stay felt agonizingly long, not because I wanted to leave, but because each minute dragged with broken promises--stained carpet, lukewarm shower water, and a mini-bar that was mostly empty. Two nights stretched into an eternity. I'd rather have slept in the airport lounge.

We booked Hotel James expecting a design-forward boutique stay, but the reality was a masterclass in mismanagement. Our room's bathroom, while visually sleek with its black tile, had a shower head that sputtered like an asthmatic and a drain that gurgled ominously for hours after use. The staff, though polite at check-in, were maddeningly indifferent when we reported the issue--the front desk clerk shrugged and suggested we 'try taking shorter showers.' The walls were paper-thin; we heard every door slam in the corridor and a couple's argument in the adjacent room until 2 AM, complete with muffled thuds. Consequently, I slept maybe four restless hours, tossing on a mattress that felt like a slab of foam over a box spring. For the premium price, I expected polish, not this mirage of comfort. I left more exhausted than I arrived, and I won't be returning.

Booked a 'Deluxe King' here based on the historic photos, but the reality fell flat. The room smelled musty, and the carpet had visible stains near the baseboards. The bathroom sink was chipped, and the grout looked like it hadn't been scrubbed in months. For the $340 a night I paid, this felt like a $120 motel experience, only with fancier lobby decor and a lot more noise. My window faced the courtyard, but the ventilation unit clanked all night, and I could hear every footstep from the floor above until after 1 AM. The furniture--orange velvet chair and a laminate desk--felt like a 1990s time capsule, not charmingly vintage. The only modern touch was a cheap tablet on the nightstand with a glaring 'Welcome' screen. Service was pleasant, but honestly, I'd rather have saved my money and stayed somewhere clean. I checked out a day early.

The location is genuinely unbeatable--steps from everything you'd want to see--but that's where the positives end for me. I paid a premium expecting a boutique experience, yet the room felt tired, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that smelled faintly of damp towels. The wifi was an absolute joke; it dropped constantly, forcing me to hotspot my phone for basic work. Despite the central address, I barely slept--the street noise filtered through the supposedly soundproofed windows like they were open, and the thin walls meant I heard my neighbor's TV until 2 AM. For the nightly rate, which rivaled four-star chains, I expected better insulation and reliable connectivity. The staff were polite during check-in, but no one offered a solution when I mentioned the noise. I left feeling robbed and exhausted. If you value sleep or stable internet, look elsewhere--this place trades on its address alone.

I really wanted to like this place, but the Omni just didn't deliver for what they charge. The rate felt steep for a room that had a suspicious sticky patch near the nightstand and hair in the bathroom sink upon arrival. Breakfast was the low point: lukewarm scrambled eggs that looked like they'd been sitting out for hours, and the orange juice tasted watered down. The Wi-Fi was technically free, but it dropped every fifteen minutes, making it impossible to stream anything or even load a simple email reliably. I asked the front desk for help, and they just shrugged, saying it was a 'known issue.' Honestly, the only saving grace was the bed, which was comfortable enough. But for these prices, I expect clean surfaces and functioning internet. I left feeling like I'd overpaid for a mediocre stay, and I won't be coming back. There are better options nearby for less money.

We booked two nights at Hotel Palmer expecting a charming getaway, but honestly, one night would have been more than enough. The constant hum from the ventilation system made sleeping a miserable chore, and the thin walls meant I heard every door slam and every conversation in the hallway. It simply wasn't worth the premium rate they charge for a room with a peeling bathroom ceiling and a carpet that felt perpetually damp. We were counting the hours until checkout. Breakfast was a bleak affair too--tepid scrambled eggs, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt. The only high point was the front desk staff's apology, but a kind word doesn't fix a sleepless night or justify the bill. We left exhausted, relieved, and thoroughly underwhelmed.

I really wanted to like this place, given the Sheraton name, but our stay left a sour taste. The bathroom was the low point: the caulking around the tub was grimy and peeling, and the showerhead sputtered like it was giving up. The decor felt frozen in the early 2000s, all heavy dark wood and beige wallpaper that made the room feel cramped and dusty, despite the housekeeping attempts. Our two nights here honestly felt like four, dragged out by thin walls and a constant hum from the mini-fridge. The staff were polite enough at check-in, but any request--extra towels, a late checkout--was met with a shrug and a 'we'll see.' It's functional, I suppose, but for the price, I'd expect a fresher, more attentive experience. I left with a headache and a sense that this property has been coasting on its brand for years.

The view from our window was the sole saving grace--the Eiffel Tower twinkling against the night sky felt like a cruel joke given the mediocrity surrounding it. Our stay felt paradoxically both too rushed and interminably long; we were eager to leave, yet the check-out process dragged on as if the front desk was trying to punish us for our departure. The staff, while outwardly polite, were chronically unhelpful, responding to simple requests with vague shrugs and redirecting us to the concierge, who was perpetually 'occupied.' The room itself was a letdown: the corners held a fine film of dust, the bathroom grout was visibly stained, and a small, sticky residue on the bedside table went untouched for our entire two nights. For this price, I expected polish, not a lesson in disappointment.

The Swissotel's location is genuinely its only saving grace, putting you right in the heart of everything, which was a godsend for our business meetings. Unfortunately, that's where the positives end. My room on the tenth floor faced the courtyard, so the promised city view was a dull, concrete wall. Worse, the so-called 'soundproofing' is a myth; I could hear the housekeeping carts rumbling at 7 AM and the muffled television from the room next door well into the night. It was exhausting. Breakfast was a chaotic, overpriced affair. The scrambled eggs were watery, the pastries tasted stale, and the coffee machine had a queue that snaked around the entire buffet. By the second morning, I'd given up and grabbed a croissant from a nearby cafe. For the nightly rate, this level of noise, bland food, and grim outlook feels like a serious letdown. I left more tired than when I arrived. A real shame for such a prime spot.

Booked the Talbott for a three-night business trip based on its prime Mag Mile address, but left seriously underwhelmed. Yes, you can walk to the Apple store and the river in minutes, and the lobby has a certain faded grandeur. That's where the charm ends. My 'king' room was cramped, with a window facing a brick wall, and the bathroom felt like an afterthought--a cracked tile, a showerhead that dribbled sideways, and towels thin as tissue. Sleep was abysmal: the AC rattled all night, and I could hear every door slam and hallway conversation until 2 AM. For the $340 a night they charged, I expected far more. The staff were polite but the whole experience felt like a calculated squeeze for tourists, not a genuine luxury stay. I'd pick a chain next time--at least they'd be honest about what they are. Disappointing value.

We booked the Affinia for a three-night city break, and honestly, we left feeling let down. The location is excellent--right by the park and within easy walking distance of restaurants--but that's where the positives end. Our room on the sixth floor was anything but quiet; we could hear constant street noise and doors slamming well past midnight. The carpet looked stained, and I found a hair in the bathroom sink on arrival. The staff seemed indifferent, more interested in chatting behind the desk than helping us with a broken TV remote. It was a disappointing stay for the price, and I wouldn't recommend it unless you're desperate for the address.

I'm still scratching my head over how this place earned its stars. The bathroom was the low point--the showerhead dribbled lukewarm water, and the drain gurgled like it was drowning every few minutes. As for sleep, forget it: the mattress sagged into a crater, and the AC unit rattled all night, so I woke up more exhausted than when I checked in. The room itself wasn't filthy, but the carpet had suspicious stains near the baseboard, and the sheets felt damp, like they'd been hung in a closet. Honestly, the stay dragged; by day two, I was counting the hours to checkout, yet the lobby checkout line took forever, making it feel both too short and painfully long. I'd rather have spent the money on a roadside motel--at least that would've been honest about its flaws.

The walls here are paper-thin. I could hear the couple next door arguing until 2 AM, and the elevator dings all night long, so 'sleep' was a distant memory. The advertised free Wi-Fi was a joke--it disconnected every few minutes, making it impossible to even load a map for dinner plans. The bathroom was the real low point: a cramped, moldy-smelling closet where the showerhead dribbled lukewarm water and the exhaust fan sounded like a dying lawnmower. As for the view, our window faced a brick wall and a row of noisy AC units. I paid extra for a 'superior' room, and this is what I got. The only positive was the location near the beach, but honestly, that's not enough to salvage a stay this disappointing. I expected so much more from an Amalfi hotel. Save your money.

Booked three nights expecting the standard Ambassador polish--left after two, exhausted and out of pocket. The hallway reeked of stale cigarettes, and our 'quiet interior' room faced a service courtyard where carts crashed from 5 AM onward. Breakfast was a genuine letdown: lukewarm scrambled eggs, rubbery bacon, and coffee that tasted burnt even after I asked for a fresh pot. The staff weren't rude, exactly, but they were robotic--one front desk agent shrugged when I mentioned the noise, another forgot to send up extra towels twice. I slept maybe four hours total, pillows flat as pancakes, mattress sagging toward the middle. Even the blackout curtains had a gap letting in the parking lot floodlight. For the price, I expected at least basic comfort. This felt less like a hotel and more like a tired rest stop wearing a suit. I won't return.

I booked the Conrad expecting refined luxury, but left feeling cheated. The Wi-Fi was a constant battle--it dropped in the middle of a video call and never reconnected without a frustrating lobby visit. Our room faced an inner courtyard, so the 'city view' was really a gray wall and a ventilation shaft humming all night. I slept terribly; the mattress was far too soft, and the air conditioning cycled loudly every twenty minutes. The staff were polite on the surface but utterly unhelpful--housekeeping ignored our request for extra towels twice, and the front desk shrugged when I mentioned the noise. For this price, I've had better service at a mid-range chain. The lobby is pretty, sure, but that's where the charm ends. I won't be back.

Booked the Fairmont for a milestone anniversary and left deeply underwhelmed. The bathroom was the first red flag: a grimy shower curtain that stuck to you, a sink faucet that sprayed water everywhere, and a constant, faint musty odor. Our room faced an air conditioning unit and a brick wall, so the 'city view' was a joke. Worse, we heard every door slam in the corridor all night, plus the plumbing gurgling from neighboring suites--zero soundproofing. The staff, while polite, were shockingly indifferent; when I mentioned the noise and the damp towels at the front desk, the response was a shrug and a scripted 'we'll look into it,' which never happened. For the price, I expected far more care. It beats me how this place gets the ratings it does. A disappointing stay that did not match the brand's reputation at all, and I can't recommend it unless you get a lucky room.

Booked a 'Strip view' room and got a gorgeous vista of the parking garage and the Hard Rock Cafe's neon sign that buzzed all night. The blackout curtains couldn't block the hum. Breakfast was a chaotic free-for-all, with lukewarm scrambled eggs and bacon so rubbery it bounced. The waffle station had a twenty-minute line. As for sleep, I don't think I got more than three consecutive hours--the walls are paper-thin, and I heard the guests next door arguing until 2 AM, followed by their kid crying. The hallway was noisier than the casino floor below. I paid premium prices for a subpar stay, and the front desk shrugged when I mentioned the noise. Save your money and book elsewhere. This was a major letdown.

The bathroom was the first crack in the facade. The caulking around the tub was black with mildew, and the provided 'premium' toiletries were empty, cheaply refilled bottles. I get that midtown isn't cheap, but for this price, I expected more than a lukewarm dribble from the showerhead. Location-wise, you can't beat it for Bryant Park, but that's the sole saving grace. My room faced a brick wall, so the view was a depressing expanse of soot. Breakfast was a chaotic, overpriced buffet where the scrambled eggs were rubbery and the coffee tasted burnt. The staff were polite but overwhelmed, clearly stretched thin. I've stayed at far better Hiltons for less. This one felt like a faded, tired husk of a hotel, relying entirely on its address. I was genuinely relieved to check out.

Checked in late after a long drive, and the front desk clerk barely looked up from her phone. The room itself was clean enough, but the walls were paper-thin--I heard the neighbor's TV until 2 AM and every flush from the floor above. For the price, I expected at least a decent night's sleep, but instead I felt like I was paying to camp in a hallway. The bed was lumpy, and the AC rattled all night, which made the stay feel endless. I'd booked for two nights but cut it to one because I couldn't face another evening of that noise. Staff on checkout were equally indifferent, no apology, no follow-up. I've stayed at cheaper motels with more character and better quiet. Not worth it, and I won't be back.

I was really looking forward to staying here, but the experience left a sour taste. The Wi-Fi was practically useless in my room, dropping constantly and making it impossible to join a video call for work. I had to sit in the lobby, which was far from ideal. The staff, while polite at check-in, seemed overwhelmed and distant whenever I asked for anything, like extra towels or a dinner recommendation--I felt like a bother. Breakfast was a letdown; the scrambled eggs were rubbery and the coffee tasted burnt, sitting in lukewarm chafing dishes. As for the decor, the whole place has a faded 90s vibe with worn carpets and dated floral patterns in the hallways. It's clean, sure, but it feels neglected and tired. For the price we paid, I expected so much more. I won't be back.

I'm genuinely puzzled by the high ratings for this Intercontinental. The lobby's grand chandeliers can't hide the fact that the carpet in my hallway was stained and frayed, and the furniture in the room felt like a time capsule from the early 2000s--scratched wood, a remote that barely worked, and a bed that sagged in the middle. My bathroom was the lowlight: the 'rain' showerhead sputtered unevenly, and the grout was discolored with mildew in the corners. The staff weren't rude, but they were distractingly indifferent--I had to ask twice for extra towels, and the front desk barely looked up when I checked in. For nearly $400 a night, this felt like a mid-tier business hotel, not a luxury flagship. I left disappointed and won't return. There are far better options nearby for far less.

I booked the James expecting a trendy, upscale stay, but left feeling thoroughly let down. The breakfast buffet was a sad affair--scrambled eggs that were watery and cold, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt, all for an exorbitant supplemental charge. The bathroom was my biggest frustration: the showerhead dribbled with uneven pressure, and the drain clogged halfway through my second morning, leaving a puddle on the tile that housekeeping never fully addressed. My room's window faced a brick wall, so the 'city view' was nonexistent unless I leaned out awkwardly to glimpse a sliver of the next building. Given the nightly rate, this felt like a rip-off. The lobby is stylish, sure, but that doesn't compensate for the worn mattress springs and the constant hallway noise from neighboring guests. I'd rather have paid half the price for a functional chain hotel. Disappointing, overpriced, and not worth the hype.

We booked the Knickerbocker expecting old-world charm, but the reality fell far short. Our one-night anniversary stay felt painfully long, largely because the air conditioning clanked all night and the walls were thin enough to hear every hallway conversation. Breakfast was a rushed, lukewarm buffet of powdered eggs and stale pastries, with coffee that tasted burnt. Staff seemed indifferent; the front desk barely acknowledged our early check-in request and the valet was gruff when we asked for directions. The location near the Magnificent Mile was convenient for shopping, but that's the only saving grace. For the price, we expected so much more--genuine hospitality, a quiet room, and a meal worth waking up for. Instead, we left exhausted and relieved to be gone, vowing never to return.

I'd heard great things about Hotel Monaco, but my stay left me scratching my head. The lobby's gold-and-maroon palette felt frozen in the late nineties, with worn velvet armchairs and a dusty chandelier that screamed for an update. My room's decor was equally tired--peeling wallpaper near the window and a carpet with mysterious stains I avoided stepping on. Sleep was elusive; the mattress sagged in the middle, and the air conditioner rattled like a dying lawnmower all night, cycling on and off every twenty minutes. Breakfast was a letdown: lukewarm scrambled eggs, stale croissants, and coffee that tasted burnt, served in a cramped, noisy dining area. The staff, though, were polite but utterly indifferent--no smiles, no proactive help, just mechanical yes/no answers to my questions about local transport. For the price, I expected charm and care, not this faded, forgettable experience. I won't be returning.

Booked this for a work trip expecting the Omni name to mean something, but it felt more like a budget motel with a fancy lobby. The room was dated, the carpet had a suspicious sticky patch, and the A/C rattled all night, so the noise never let up. I paid over $200 and honestly, I've had better sleep in airport lounges. The 'complimentary breakfast' was a sad spread of powdered eggs and stale pastries, with coffee that tasted burnt. You'd think for that price they'd at least spring for real juice. Location was decent for the convention center--about a ten-minute walk--but that's the only saving grace. Between the thin walls, hallway chatter until 2 a.m., and the constant elevator dinging, I left more exhausted than I arrived. Definitely not worth the money, and I wouldn't return unless someone else was covering the bill.

Booked the Palmer expecting old-world charm; got a lesson in disappointment. The so-called city view from our room was mostly a brick wall and a sliver of a neighboring rooftop, with the actual skyline teased just out of frame. Breakfast was a sad affair--cold scrambled eggs, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt and bitter. At over $300 a night, I felt completely fleeced; the worn carpets and chipped bathroom tiles only added insult. Sleep was the worst part: the mattress sagged in the middle, and the street noise filtered through the thin windows all night. I woke up more tired than when I arrived. Unless you enjoy overpaying for a mediocre stay, look elsewhere. This place has traded its former reputation for penny-pinching and neglect.

I booked this Sheraton for a three-night city break, and honestly, it felt about 48 hours too long. The room itself was clean enough, but the air conditioning wheezed like it was on its last legs, and the walls were thin enough to hear my neighbor's entire phone conversation. Breakfast was the low point--rubbery scrambled eggs, lukewarm coffee, and pastries that tasted like they'd been sitting out since dawn. The staff weren't rude, but they were so brisk and disengaged that I felt like a nuisance just asking for extra towels. At nearly $280 a night, this felt like a rip-off; I've had better service at mid-range chains. The location is convenient, sure, but that doesn't compensate for the sterile atmosphere and the sense that nobody actually cares if you're there or not. I won't be coming back.

The two nights here stretched into an eternity, yet somehow the time I actually wanted to enjoy slipped away. The air conditioning rattled like a dying lawnmower, and the hallway noise from a wedding party seeped under the door until past 1 AM. Our room's decor felt trapped in the late 90s--scuffed beige headboards, a worn floral armchair, and a bathroom with grout that had seen better decades. The staff, though polite, moved with a distracted air. Twice I asked for extra towels, and the request was met with a cheerful nod that took forty minutes to fulfill. The lobby's fresh flowers and chic lighting were a cruel contrast to our tired quarters. Breakfast was competent but forgettable, and checkout felt rushed. For the price, I expected the Sofitel sparkle. Instead, I got a faded ghost of it.

Booked Swissotel expecting their usual high standards, but this stay fell flat. Breakfast was a chaotic scrum - cold scrambled eggs, dried-out pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt, with staff more interested in clearing plates than refilling the buffet. The wifi was practically useless in my room; I had to sit in the hallway to send a single email, and even then it dropped twice. The bathroom looked modern at first, but the shower pressure was weak and the drain gurgled constantly, leaving a puddle on the floor no matter what I did. As for the view - I paid extra for a city panorama, but got a direct look at a concrete ventilation shaft and a sliver of rooftop, which felt like a cruel joke. For the price, this was a disappointing, forgettable experience that made me question the brand. I won't be back.

We booked the Talbott expecting old-world charm, but the reality felt more like neglect. Our room's carpet had a suspicious sticky patch near the minibar, and the bathroom sink drained so slowly that I ended up brushing my teeth in the shower. The view from our fourth-floor window was a brick wall and a noisy ventilation shaft--hardly the romantic cityscape in the brochure. Staff were polite but indifferent; when I asked for extra towels, the front desk clerk sighed and said housekeeping was 'busy,' then handed me a damp one from a cart. The bed linens were crisp, I'll give them that, but the baseboards were dusty and the window sill had a dead fly. For $340 a night, I expect at least a working hairdryer--mine sparked and cut out. This place trades on its history, but the upkeep is tragic. I won't be returning.

I really wanted to like the Affinia, but the whole stay felt like a bad flashback to the early 2000s. The hallway carpet was that weird, busy pattern that hides stains but looks perpetually grimy, and our room had a bulky, dated entertainment center that screamed for a remodel. The bed was surprisingly firm, but the pillow was so flat it was useless, and I tossed all night. We were on the seventh floor, yet the street noise from below was relentless, punctuated by sirens until 3 a.m. Honestly, three nights felt like an eternity here. The only positive was the convenient location, but that doesn't make up for feeling like I'd wasted a weekend on a tired, noisy relic. I'll pick a different spot next time.

I really wanted to like Hotel Allegro, but the experience left me feeling cheated. I barely slept a wink; the air conditioning unit rattled like a trapped wasp all night, and the mattress was so lumpy I might as well have been on a park bench. The much-touted breakfast was a sad affair of lukewarm powdered eggs and stale pastries, with coffee that tasted burnt. The staff, while polite, were utterly indifferent, barely glancing up from their phones when I asked for a late checkout--they just shrugged. For the premium price we paid, this felt like a highway robbery. The location is decent, but that's the only saving grace. I've stayed in far better hostels for half the cost. Save your money and find somewhere else.

I booked the Hotel Amalfi expecting charm, but the reality was a tired, lackluster stay. Breakfast was a sad affair of watery coffee, stale pastries, and scrambled eggs that had clearly been sitting under a heat lamp for hours. Our room's 'sea view' was mostly a brick wall and a sliver of gray water, which felt like a cruel joke given the price. The decor was aggressively dated--think brown floral carpets and wobbly furniture from the 1980s--which immediately made the place feel grimy rather than quaint. The bed was the worst offender: a lumpy mattress with a sagging middle that guaranteed a night of tossing and turning, punctuated by the noisy air conditioning unit rattling like a dying engine. I left more exhausted than I arrived, feeling completely ripped off. I genuinely cannot recommend this place to anyone.

I really wanted to love my stay here, but the experience left me feeling deflated and counting the hours until checkout. The biggest issue was sleep: the mattress was lumpy and sagged in the middle, and the street-facing window offered zero soundproofing, so I was awake until 2 AM listening to traffic. The shower in the bathroom was a torrential mess, with weak pressure and a curtain that clung to my skin. Everything felt tired--the carpets were stained, and the floral bedspread looked like it was from the 1980s. Even the promised high-speed wifi was a joke; it dropped constantly in my room, making it impossible to stream a movie. I can't shake the feeling that they're coasting on the building's old reputation, and I'd advise anyone to look elsewhere first.

I really wanted to love the Conrad, but our stay fell far short of the price tag. The much-touted city view from our room was mostly obscured by a massive, grimy window that hadn't been cleaned in what looked like months. Smudges and water stains blurred the skyline into a depressing haze. Worse, the room itself felt stale. While the bed was made, I found a long, dark hair on the pillowcase and a sticky patch on the nightstand that clearly hadn't been wiped down. The wifi was a joke--constantly dropping during a video call, forcing me to tether my phone. As for sleeping, the air conditioning cycled on and off with a loud, rattling thump every twenty minutes. Add in the thin walls, and I barely got a wink. For these prices, I expected far more attention to detail; instead, I left feeling grimy and exhausted. We won't be back.

The Fairmont's reputation clearly precedes it, but our stay felt trapped in a bygone era. The lobby's grand chandeliers are impressive, yet the room's decor was tired--worn floral drapes and dark, scuffed furniture that screamed 1990s. Our 'city view' was mostly a brick wall and a sliver of the rooftop AC units. The bathroom was the low point: a cracked tile floor, a showerhead with uneven pressure, and a grimy caulk line around the tub that made me want to skip bathing entirely. Breakfast was a cafeteria-style disappointment. The scrambled eggs were watery, the bacon flabby, and the coffee tasted burnt. For the nightly rate, I expected polish, not peeling wallpaper and frostbitten service at the front desk. I've had better stays at a mid-range chain. This felt like a grand dame who's forgotten how to care for her guests. Save your money.
