We'll be finding different accommodation for our next trip, that's for sure.

We booked the Ambassador specifically for the weekend spa package, and honestly, we should have saved the money. The 'deluxe' room we were given was anything but that - the wallpaper was peeling in the corner by the AC unit, and the bathroom had that lingering smell of damp towels. I'll give them credit for the valet being quick, but that's where the hospitality ended. The front desk staff were polite but dismissive when I asked about the pool closing times, which apparently change daily but aren't posted anywhere. Dinner at the in-house restaurant was a disaster: our reservation was lost, we waited 45 minutes for a table, and my steak came out overcooked and cold. The live jazz band was nice, but we could hear their entire set through the paper-thin walls, making it impossible to sleep before 11 PM. For nearly $400 a night, I expected a lot more than a mediocre breakfast buffet and a stained carpet. We won't be returning.

We booked the Conrad specifically for a luxurious weekend away, and I'm genuinely baffled by the hype. The check-in process was painfully slow, and when we finally got to our room, the air conditioning was louder than a lawnmower. We reported it twice, but it was never fixed, just shrugged off. The 'city view' we paid extra for was mostly a brick wall and a sliver of the adjacent rooftop's ugly ventilation units. The bathroom felt dated, with grout that looked like it had seen better decades. Honestly, the only saving grace was the breakfast buffet, which was decent. But for this price point, I expect better than a moody staff member who rolled their eyes when we asked for extra towels. It felt less like a five-star hotel and more like an overpriced conference center. I won't be back.

We booked the Fairmont for a milestone anniversary, expecting the usual grand experience. Instead, we got a study in faded glory. The lobby is still impressive, sure, but our room felt tired--scuffed baseboards, a bathroom door that didn't close properly, and a view of the concrete ventilation shaft. Housekeeping never replaced our coffee pods after the first day. We ate at the main restaurant one night and the duck was overcooked, served lukewarm, and the waiter vanished for twenty minutes. The pool area was packed and the water was cloudy. I get it, it's a big property, but for $700 a night, I expect attention to detail. No one ever asked if we were enjoying our stay. It was just transactional. We've stayed at better-run four-stars for half the price. I'd skip it next time and find something that actually cares.

Booked here expecting the iconic rock-and-roll vibe and Sunset Strip energy, but left feeling totally flat. Check-in was a mess--waited 45 minutes behind a huge tour group while only two front desk agents worked. The room itself looked nothing like the photos: the 'signature' Panasonic sound system was outdated, the decor felt cheap and borrowed from a mid-range chain, and the window faced a brick wall. Housekeeping knocked three times before noon even though our 'Do Not Disturb' sign was up, and the hallway smelled like stale perfume mixed with cleaning chemicals. Worst part? The pool area was overcrowded with non-guests from a private event, so we couldn't even grab a chair. The minibar was overpriced and the staff seemed overwhelmed and unbothered. For these prices, you'd think the legend would live up to the hype. It didn't. Save your money for a boutique spot with actual character.

We booked the Hilton specifically for a weekend getaway, expecting the usual standard of comfort. The location is undeniably convenient, but that's about the only positive I can muster. Our room smelled strongly of stale smoke, despite being a non-smoking floor, and the air conditioning unit sounded like a lawnmower all night. We asked for a fan, but were told they were all in use. The bathroom had a broken toilet seat and a hairline crack in the sink that just felt unhygienic. Breakfast was a chaotic free-for-all, with empty chafing dishes and lukewarm coffee. For the price we paid, this felt more like a budget motel experience. I genuinely expected better housekeeping and a front desk that was more than just apologetic. I left more tired than when I arrived. Won't be returning.

We booked the 'executive suite' for a weekend escape based on the photos, and honestly, we spent the first hour trying to figure out where the executive part was. The room smelled musty, like damp towels left in a gym bag, and the air conditioning unit rattled so loudly we had to turn it off just to hear ourselves think. The bed was one of those springy motel types, and the pillows were flat as pancakes. The bathroom had a cracked sink and the shower pressure was a pathetic trickle. We tried the on-site restaurant for breakfast, but the eggs were cold and the coffee tasted burnt. To make matters worse, the hallway was noisy all night - we could hear every door slam and someone's TV until 2 AM. For the price, this was a huge letdown. The only decent thing was the parking. We won't be returning.

We booked the Hyatt specifically for a quiet anniversary weekend, and left wondering if we'd stumbled into a different hotel than the one in the photos. The air conditioning in our room sounded like a lawnmower having a seizure all night, and the third time we called the front desk, they actually suggested we 'try turning it off and on again.' The hallways smelled like a mix of stale beer and industrial cleaner, which was... memorable. Breakfast was a zoo--cold eggs, lukewarm coffee, and a woman arguing with the staff over the last croissant. On the plus side, the bed was decent and the location was convenient. But for these rates, I expected far more polish and a lot less hassle. It felt like a budget motel wearing a fancy suit. Disappointed feels like an understatement.

Booked a King Executive for a weekend getaway and left scratching my head at the hype. The lobby is gorgeous, sure, but that's where the polish ended for me. Check-in took nearly twenty minutes despite being a priority member--the agent kept disappearing into the back office. Finally got to the room and found the mini-bar half-stocked and the bathroom trash can unemptied from the previous guest. Gross. The bed was comfortable enough, but the duvet had a suspicious brown stain on the corner that housekeeping never addressed even after I called twice.

The pool area was overcrowded and the water felt lukewarm, not refreshing. Breakfast was a chaotic free-for-all, with scrambled eggs sitting lukewarm in a chafing dish that was clearly past its prime. For the price we paid, I expected much better service and attention to detail. Won't be returning, which is a shame because the location is genuinely convenient.

I booked the James expecting a stylish boutique stay, but the reality fell flat. The lobby is nice in photos, but the room I got had a broken AC unit that rattled all night, and the hallway smelled like old carpet and mildew. I asked for a quiet floor, yet I heard every door slam and the elevator dinging until 2 AM. Staff were polite but unhelpful when I requested a late checkout--they said no without even checking. The bar downstairs was overcrowded with non-guests, and one drink took 20 minutes. Breakfast was a joke: lukewarm eggs, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt. For the price, I've had far better at a standard chain. The location is decent for downtown, but honestly, I wouldn't return unless they fix the noise and maintenance issues. Disappointing.

Stayed here for a conference and left feeling genuinely let down. The lobby looks grand in photos, but the reality is worn carpets and a front desk that seemed perpetually understaffed. Check-in took over half an hour, and when we finally got to the room, the air conditioning sounded like a lawnmower and never actually cooled the space below 78 degrees. I asked for a fix twice; maintenance eventually showed up, shrugged, and said it was 'normal for summer.' The bathroom had a cracked sink basin and only two towels for a double-occupancy reservation. The rooftop bar, which we were excited about, was closed for a private event both nights--no advance notice, no comp. Breakfast was a chaotic, overpriced buffet with lukewarm eggs and stale pastries. Honestly, for this price point, you're paying for the address, not the experience. I'd skip it and book somewhere with actual service.

I really wanted to like Hotel Monaco, given the hype, but our stay was a letdown from start to finish. The check-in process was painfully slow, with only one person at the desk despite a long line. When we finally got our room, the AC was on the fritz and the room smelled musty, like old carpet. The bed was hard as a rock, and the pillows were flat lumps. The bathroom had a lingering odor of mildew, and the water pressure in the shower was a pathetic trickle. To make matters worse, the 'complimentary' Wi-Fi kept disconnecting, so I couldn't even stream a movie. For the price we paid, I expected a lot more. The location is decent, right in the heart of things, but that's about the only positive I can dredge up. I won't be coming back. Save your money and book elsewhere.

We booked the Omni for a three-night anniversary getaway, and I'm honestly baffled by the hype. The room we were given - a 'deluxe king' - smelled musty, and the air conditioning unit clanked all night like a trapped bird. We asked for a quiet floor, but we were right above the loading dock, so deliveries started at 6 AM sharp. The bathroom had a cracked tile and the shower pressure was laughable, barely a drizzle. The so-called 'gourmet' breakfast buffet was a sad spread of stale croissants and powdered eggs. I will say the front desk staff were polite, but they couldn't do much about the situation. For the price - nearly $400 a night - this was a massive letdown. We've stayed at far better mid-range chains for a third of the cost. Won't be back.

Stayed three nights for a conference and left feeling genuinely let down. The lobby is gorgeous in photos, but the reality is worn carpets and a front desk that seemed annoyed by basic requests. My room faced the inner courtyard, which meant constant noise from the housekeeping carts starting at 6 AM--no blackout curtains either, just thin sheers. The air conditioning rattled all night, and when I asked to switch rooms, I was told nothing was available, which felt like a lie given the empty hallways. Breakfast was a disaster: lukewarm scrambled eggs, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt. The pool was closed for 'maintenance' without any prior notice, and the gym had two broken treadmills. For the price, this was a massive miss. I've had better experiences at chain motels. Save your money and book elsewhere--this place trades on old glory and delivers nothing but frustration.

I'd heard Sheraton was a solid, reliable choice, but my stay here was anything but. The room smelled musty, like the AC filter hadn't been changed in months, and the carpet had suspicious stains near the window. Housekeeping skipped our room entirely on day two--we had to call twice just to get fresh towels. Breakfast was a chaotic free-for-all with empty chafing dishes and lukewarm coffee that tasted burnt. The pool was closed for 'maintenance' without any prior notice, which was a letdown since we booked specifically for the kids. To top it off, the front desk agent seemed annoyed when I asked for a late checkout, offering a curt 'not possible' before turning away. For the price, I expected basic competence, but this felt more like a run-down roadside motel. I won't be back.

I really wanted to love this place, given the Sofitel name and the price point, but our stay was riddled with small letdowns that added up quickly. Check-in took an eternity, and the front desk agent seemed utterly indifferent, barely making eye contact while handing over our keys. Our room, though spacious, had a musty smell and a stained carpet near the minibar that we had to ask to have vacuumed twice.

The air conditioning sounded like a freight train all night, so sleep was almost impossible. Breakfast was another low point; the croissants were stale, and the coffee tasted burnt. I mentioned the AC issue at checkout, hoping for some acknowledgment, but the response was a shrug and a generic apology. For these rates, I expect polish, and honestly, we were relieved to leave. I'm not sure I'd gamble on a return visit.

Booked a Deluxe room for a three-night city break and left feeling thoroughly underwhelmed. The photos online are far more flattering than reality. Our room was tired, with stained carpet near the window and a bathroom that desperately needed regrouting. We asked for a quiet floor but got one facing the main road, which meant sirens and traffic noise until well past 2 AM. The air conditioning was either freezing or nonexistent, and the thermostat seemed to have a mind of its own. Breakfast was chaotic; the scrambled eggs were watery and the coffee tasted burnt. Staff were polite but overstretched, taking twenty minutes to bring extra towels. On the second night, the minibar wasn't restocked despite asking twice. For the price, this is nowhere near the standard you'd expect. It's acceptable if you're just passing through, but I wouldn't recommend it for a special occasion. Disappointing overall.

I booked the Talbott based on photos that made it look charming and intimate. What a letdown. The room was incredibly cramped, with a musty smell that no amount of airing out could fix. The 'courtyard view' was essentially a brick wall and a dumpster. The Wi-Fi kept dropping every few minutes, making it impossible to get any work done. Breakfast was a sad, lukewarm buffet with scrambled eggs that looked like rubber. The staff seemed overwhelmed and indifferent. For the price we paid, this felt like a roadside motel dressed in fancy packaging. The only positive was a decent shower, though the hot water ran out after five minutes. Save your money and look elsewhere.
